reported control transfers in May-Jul. 2016"}]} Notes [1] A cooptee is an MSS collaborator, whom the ministry uses for operational support—typically in exchange for favors. They can help make introductions, serve as a go-between for the MSS and a source, provide excuses for sources to travel to the PRC, or otherwise assist the MSS in its operations. The MSS may also approach these people because of the access, business, or other ability that they have to support operations ( National Interest , June 11, 2017). [2] In November 2014, CITIC Securities (中信证券) bought a 3.8 percent stake in a technology firm under a stock return swap with Hexi, helping Gu gain control of the listed company ( CSRC , May 12, 2017). Ms. Huang worked in securities financing at CITIC at the time. The deal may have brought her into contact with Kang a year before she joined Hexi ( Hexi Investment , March 17, 2017). [3] In 2014, Hexi subscribed for shares in Century Huatong connected to its acquisitions of Tianyou Software (天游软件) and Wuxi SevenCool (无锡七酷网络). In 2017, Wuxi SevenCool sold the gaming company Hangzhou Shengfeng (杭州盛锋) to Ningbo Jingxuan (宁波镜瑄), whose ultimate controller is Kang (CNINF, March 9, 2014 , March 7, 2017 ). [4] The name of this firm, Shanghai Lingsu (上海凌素), closely resembles another firm within Ms. Huang’s business network, Shanghai Lingsuda (上海领素达), which invests primarily in smart mobility and ride-hailing platforms (see the Interactive Map) ( CAIC , August 16, 2023; Hong Kong Exchange , December 23, 2024). Yunxi also entered the ownership chain of a data center holding company, also based in Shanghai, and in 2025 changed its own registered name to Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing Data Group (上海珑腾智算数据集团) ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 13, 2023; Times Weekly , November 9). In Shanghai business circles, it is common to register a series of companies with names that share the same Chinese characters or use different characters with the same pronunciation. Other businesspeople can then easily tell who actually controls a company from its name alone. [5] Kang had previously used companies he controlled, including Hexi, to take over three major Phicomm shareholding vehicles ( Sina Finance , August 10, 2018). [6] Such data centers under Kang’s control, with refurbishment nearing completion, would very likely use Nvidia chips smuggled into the PRC through Huang’s Megaspeed. [7] The business tactic of offering one’s spouse to another man reaches even much further back. During the Warring States period, Zichu (子楚), a prince of Qin (秦), took an interest in Zhao Ji (赵姬), the consort of the merchant Lu Buwei (吕不韦). Lu, considering how much he had already bet on Zichu to be the next King of Qin, offered Zhao Ji, who was already pregnant, to him. After Zichu became king of Qin, Lu was appointed chancellor and wielded power over the Qin court ( Records of the Grand Historian , accessed November 11). A historical conspiracy theory even held that Qin Shi Huang (秦始皇), first emperor of ancient China, was Lu and Zhao Ji’s son. In the early 2010s, PRC financial media and business books often portrayed Lu Buwei as a merchant who knew how to bet on real power (through whatever means), fueling an interest in him among businessmen of the era (see Fortune China , March 23, 2011). That was precisely when Kang rose to prominence in business. The post Alice Huang’s Shady Shanghai Ties to Business and Government appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Community-Focused Academic Brings AI Tools to Colorado Farmers
zh_title: 以社区为中心的学术界为科罗拉多州农民带来人工智能工具
summary: 科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”东 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县扩建项目 Tit
content:
科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”董 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县推广 职称 推广区域专家 会员等级 高级会员 母校内蒙古师范大学，位于呼和浩特；北京师范大学；纽约州立大学环境科学与林业学院，位于锡拉丘兹；科罗拉多州立大学全球分校 她构建了人工智能驱动的农业旅游聊天机器人 (AgriTourismAI.com)，帮助农民和牧场主启动和经营“农业旅游”业务。农业旅游是指农民向游客开放他们的土地以进行娱乐、教育或购物活动。常见的例子包括采摘自己的果园、如何种植蔬菜的课程以及手工产品的销售。董还举办研讨会，向农民和牧场主展示如何使用人工智能工具来帮助发展和管理他们的业务。她说她将自己视为大学和农村之间的纽带。 “我们（推广专家）充当桥梁，”她说。
“我们将校园与我们服务的农村社区联系起来。”许多农民和牧场主年龄较大，通常没有接受过技术培训。他们的子孙常常离开农场到城市工作，或者无法教他们新工具。如果没有帮助，人工智能的好处可能会与农民失之交臂。 Dong 的研讨会为他们提供了一条出路。Dong 凭借她的 AgriPivot AI Agent 入围 2026 年 GenAI for Good Challenge 决赛。该挑战赛由 IEEE Humanarian Technologies 和联合国国际电信联盟组织，她的项目是从 79 个国家的 318 个团队中选出的。她还获得了国家推广技术社区 (NETC) 颁发的 2026 年创新奖，以及国家社区发展推广专业人员协会 (NACDEP) 颁发的 2025 年国家和西部地区教育技术奖。作为首席研究员或联合首席研究员，她获得了七项竞争性资助，总额超过 25 万美元，其中包括由农业部国家食品和农业研究所支持的资金。董出生于北京，从小就热爱设计和解决问题。她的父母都是医生。小时候，她喜欢画新的、有创意的东西。她说，素描可以让她用图片解决脑海中的问题，并将它们作为实际设计写在纸上。这个习惯逐渐成为她与周围环境相处的一种方式。
她说：“我一直热衷于创造一些有形的东西来解决现实世界中的问题。”她并不将自己的人生方向归功于任何一位导师。相反，她说她所有的老师都帮助她为她的职业生涯奠定了基础。她就读于位于呼和浩特的内蒙古师范大学，这是一所培训教师的机构。 2013 年，她在那里获得了两个学士学位——一个是地理科学学士学位，另一个是教育学士学位。然后，她获得了课程和教学硕士学位

【原文 English Original】
Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension , CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there. Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan County Title Extension regional specialist Member grade Senior member Alma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products. Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business. She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside. “We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in. Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and the U.N.’s International Telecommunication Union , and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC) , and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP). She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture . An early love of design and problem-solving Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors. As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs. That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings. “I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says. She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career. She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University , in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education. She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016. That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry , in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020. From outreach to extension work After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College , in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator. She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water. She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain , helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park. In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County ’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns. She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds. Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System , a nationwide network run by land-grant universities , schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states. The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture , managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties. The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program , which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship. Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person. She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says. “We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says. Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI . The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly. How her AI chatbot helps farmers and ranchers In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree , in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global . She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python , a popular programming language . It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT ’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it. The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download. Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk. One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch , in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases . Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication. Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) . The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing. She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude , and Gemini . She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp ., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp ., Colorado Startup Week , and Boulder Startup Week . And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel. Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools , she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use. She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says. Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.” How IEEE membership supports her career Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology . She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group . IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences. IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.” She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE. Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone. “They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

title: Mysterious MQ-25 Stingray-Like Chinese Drone Emerges At Little-Known Flight Test Center
zh_title: 神秘的MQ-25类似黄貂鱼的中国无人机出现在鲜为人知的飞行测试中心
summary: 卫星图像显示，中国浦城有一架不寻常的无人驾驶飞机，其配置与波音公司的舰载 MQ-25 Stingray 非常相似。虽然我们仍然不知道无人机的功能，但该设施本身似乎也成为中国不断扩大的无人驾驶飞机工业的一个日益重要的枢纽。 Vantor 向 TWZ 提供的宽视野卫星图像显示了 2026 年 4 月 23 日位于浦城的神秘无人机。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 这架无人机最初在浦城内府机场的卫星图像中被发现后引起了人们的关注。

卫星图像显示，中国浦城有一架不寻常的无人驾驶飞机，其配置与波音公司的舰载 MQ-25 Stingray 非常相似。虽然我们仍然不知道无人机的功能，但该设施本身似乎也成为中国不断扩大的无人驾驶飞机工业的一个日益重要的枢纽。 Vantor 向 TWZ 提供的一张广角卫星图像显示了 2026 年 4 月 23 日在蒲城的神秘无人机。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 这架无人机最初引起了人们的关注，因为它在中国西北部陕西省蒲城内府机场的卫星图像中被发现，可通过苹果地图查看。无人机出现在跑道上的单独图像也可以通过必应地图获得。 TWZ 随后从 Vantor 获得了浦城的图像，显​​示了相关无人驾驶飞机。真是一个惊喜！苹果地图上发现三架无人机出现在蒲城。 CH-7、九天和类似MQ-25的无人机。 pic.twitter.com/rREqLuFAdU — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) 2026 年 11 月 18 日再次出现在 bing 地图上！这次它出现在跑道上 pic.twitter.com/xLgZetmOZf — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) 2026 年 11 月 19 日 除了不明飞行器之外，今年 4 月从蒲城拍摄的图像还揭示了似乎是 CH-7 隐形飞翼无人机和重型喷气动力九天母舰无人机的例子。 2026 年 4 月 23 日，一架 CH-7 停泊在蒲城。
卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 2026 年 4 月 23 日在蒲城的九天无人机母舰。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 与不明飞行器最明显的比较是波音的 MQ-25 Stingray。 MQ-25是一种舰载无人飞机，主要为美国海军飞机提供空中加油，扩大舰载机联队的航程和操作灵活性。它还为未来无人海军航空能力奠定了基础。范托称，就尺寸而言，这架身份不明的中国无人机翼展约为66英尺，长度为49英尺。相比之下，MQ-25 的翼展约为 75 英尺，长度约为 51 英尺。 MQ-25 黄貂鱼。波音公司的这款中国无人机似乎具有相似的总体设计类别，但现阶段存在一些值得注意的重要差异。最引人注目的之一是前机身。与MQ-25不同，MQ-25的前部具有相对扁平的铲状外观，中国飞机似乎有一个更传统的锥形机头。也许这可以包含一个容纳雷达设备的锥形天线罩。这个理论，而且它只是一个理论，可以通过机头与黄色底漆机身的不同颜色来支持。进气量也不同。
与 MQ-25 相关的异国情调的齐平进气道不同，中国设计有一个更传统的背部进气道，看起来呈锯齿状，有助于雷达信号和/或分成两个通道。另一种可能性是飞机有两个发动机，尽管基于明显的分叉进气道，这仍然是推测性的。左侧浦城图像中的无人机和 MQ-25 的并排视图，提供了它们入口的比较视图。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor/Boeing 尾部配置也可能很独特，具有横向展开的 V 型尾翼，如 MQ-25，但可能采用可见控制面，而不是全移动水平尾翼设计。综合起来，这些功能

【原文 English Original】
Satellite imagery has revealed an unusual uncrewed aircraft at Pucheng, China, with a configuration that bears very strong similarities to Boeing’s carrier-based MQ-25 Stingray . While we still have no idea about the function of the drone, the facility itself also appears to be an increasingly important hub for China’s expanding uncrewed aircraft industry . A wider-view satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor shows the mystery drone at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The drone initially attracted attention after being spotted in a satellite image of Pucheng Neifu Airport in Shaanxi Province, in northwestern China, available through Apple Maps. A separate image of the drone, where it appears on a runway, is also available through Bing Maps. TWZ subsequently obtained imagery of Pucheng from Vantor showing the uncrewed aircraft in question. what a suprise! Three UAV spotted at Pucheng on apple maps. CH-7, Jiutian and a MQ-25 like UAV. pic.twitter.com/rREqLuFAdU — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 18, 2026 spotted again on bing maps! and it's on the runway this time pic.twitter.com/xLgZetmOZf — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 19, 2026 As well as the unidentified aircraft, imagery from Pucheng dating from April of this year also reveals what appears to be a CH-7 stealthy flying-wing drone and an example of the heavyweight jet-powered Jiutian mothership drone . A CH-7 at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor A Jiutian drone mothership at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The most obvious comparison for the unidentified aircraft is Boeing’s MQ-25 Stingray. The MQ-25 is a carrier-based uncrewed aircraft developed primarily to provide aerial refueling for U.S. Navy aircraft, extending the range and operational flexibility of carrier air wings. It also provides a foundation for future uncrewed naval aviation capabilities . In terms of dimensions, the unidentified Chinese UAV has a wingspan of approximately 66 feet and a length of 49 feet, according to Vantor. In contrast, the MQ-25 measures approximately 75 feet in wingspan and 51 feet in length. MQ-25 Stingray. Boeing The Chinese drone appears to occupy a similar general design category, but there are several important differences notable at this stage. One of the most noticeable is the forward fuselage. Unlike the MQ-25, whose forward section has a relatively flattened, shovel-like appearance, the Chinese aircraft appears to have a more conventional, tapered nose. Perhaps this could incorporate a conical radome housing radar equipment. That theory, and it is just a theory, could be supported by the different color of the nose compared to the yellow primer-painted airframe. The air intake is also different. Rather than the exotic, flush inlet associated with the MQ-25 , the Chinese design has a more conventional dorsal intake that appears serrated to help with radar signature and/or split into two channels. Another possibility is that the aircraft has two engines, although that remains speculative, based on the apparent bifurcated intake. A side-by-side look at the drone seen in the image of Pucheng, at left, and an MQ-25, offering comparative views of their inlets. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/Boeing The tail configuration may also be distinctive, with a laterally flared V-tail, like the MQ-25, but possibly incorporating visible control surfaces instead of an all-moving tailplane design. Taken together, these features suggest an aircraft that shares some of the MQ-25’s general design philosophy but is not an attempt at a direct clone. Long-time Chinese aerospace observer and TWZ contributor Andreas Rupprecht , who has been following developments surrounding the aircraft, believes China could be following a development path similar to Boeing’s, potentially producing a carrier-based uncrewed aerial refueling platform that can also undertake intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. “I think China is actually following the same path as Boeing here, and it’s heading towards a tanker that can also take on other roles as an ISR platform,” Rupprecht told us. A radar-equipped aircraft with substantial endurance could potentially perform surveillance and other sensor-related missions when not being used as a tanker. The potential development of a multirole uncrewed tanker at Pucheng would also fit into a much broader push by China to expand the role of uncrewed aircraft in its naval aviation forces. One of the most notable developments is the GJ-21 , a navalized derivative of the GJ-11 Sharp Sword stealth uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV). Featuring folding wings and provisions for catapult launches and arrested recoveries, the low-observable flying-wing design is intended to operate from China’s growing fleet of large-deck warships , including the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . In October 2026, Chinese state media reported that the GJ-21 had successfully completed its first takeoff and landing aboard the vessel, a significant milestone in the development of shipborne fixed-wing combat drones. GJ-21 carrier-based UCAV. via Chinese internet The GJ-21 effort is taking place alongside the introduction of China’s new catapult-equipped Fujian aircraft carrier, which has begun operating the J-35 stealth fighter, J-15T carrier-based fighter, and KJ-600 airborne early warning aircraft. Taken together, these developments point to an increasingly ambitious effort to integrate uncrewed aircraft into China’s future carrier air wings , potentially spanning stealthy strike platforms, surveillance systems, and other specialized support aircraft. The unidentified Pucheng aircraft could represent another, quite different part of that wider effort — or something else altogether. At the same time, this aircraft is roughly 20 percent dimensionally smaller than the MQ-25, which would mean it would have less fuel to give. It’s also worth noting that Boeing’s MQ-25 emerged from an unmanned combat air vehicle (UCAV) design that included low-observable features. Multirole UCAV concepts predating it also looked very similar. The MRE concept from Lockheed during the 1990s looks very similar to the MQ-25 we know today. (Lockheed Martin) In addition, Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), for instance, the FQ-42 Vengeance, and also the XQ-67 Off-Board Sensing Station share a similar overall design. With this in mind, and remembering its different nose section, this could just as easily be a true multirole UCAV or even a CCA, such as one designed for force protection of high-value aerial assets, and it may not even be carrier-capable. Rupprecht cautioned that the manufacturer of the mystery drone remains unidentified. However, one of the more interesting clues about the aircraft’s possible origins comes from Shenyang Aircraft Corporation (SAC). Rupprecht pointed to a propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025, which he believes could fit the development lineage of the larger aircraft now visible at Pucheng. The sub-scale propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025. The background reads (rough translation): “Rollout Ceremony for Final Assembly of Shenyang’s First ‘Surrogate Flight Test’ Pilot-Test Verification Platform UAV.” via Chinese internet A smaller, propeller-driven demonstrator could provide a relatively inexpensive way to investigate aerodynamic characteristics, autonomous flight controls, mission systems, and other technologies before progressing to a much larger aircraft. This piston-powered, propeller-driven aircraft with a broadly similar configuration to the MQ-25 was seen in a video flying, as well. 突然想起中国一家民营无人机公司，做过一款MQ-25活塞桨叶版 https://t.co/Y69dfzpLNS pic.twitter.com/IzU08PC8DK — 飞刀 (@chaoyinsukandao) November 18, 2026 Whether the Pucheng aircraft is related to this SAC demonstrator or if it’s an entirely separate program remains unknown. Beyond the external resemblance, there are no indications that they are linked, and the aircraft could just be a general test surrogate platform. The configuration isn’t totally novel in the advanced UAS world. The aircraft’s appearance is also interesting given the location where it has been spotted. Pucheng Neifu Airport is located in Shaanxi Province, and its surrounding aviation facilities include an area identified in Apple Maps as the National Aeronautics Industrial Base Pucheng General Aviation Industrial Park Guanliban. The industrial park has its own smaller runway, separate from the main airport infrastructure. A close-up of Pucheng with no drones visible, as of June 16, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 The site had remained relatively obscure to outside observers until roughly the past one to two years, according to Rupprecht. More recently, however, various aircraft manufacturers have apparently been conducting testing there. This raises the possibility that Pucheng is not simply an individual manufacturer’s flight-test location, but a facility used by multiple organizations developing and evaluating uncrewed aircraft. Rupprecht also raised the possibility that Pucheng could potentially be a specialized uncrewed aircraft testing facility associated with China’s Flight Test Establishment at Xi’an, commonly known as CFTE. “I cannot say (yet) whether this — and this is my theory — is effectively a branch of the CFTE at Xi’an, which is for crewed and this is a base for uncrewed ones,” Rupprecht explained. A satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor provides an overview of Pucheng as of April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor If Pucheng does serve as a shared testing location for multiple manufacturers, it could help explain the appearance of several otherwise unrelated UAV designs at the same site. Returning to the mystery drone, the combination of its apparent size, configuration, and possible connection to earlier Chinese demonstrator programs makes it an interesting development to watch. Regardless, for now, the imagery from Pucheng offers a glimpse of a potentially significant new Chinese uncrewed aircraft program. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post Mysterious MQ-25 Stingray-Like Chinese Drone Emerges At Little-Known Flight Test Center appeared first on TWZ .

﻿ 以下是上周西太平洋主要舰船活动和演习的摘要。 2026 年 11 月 11 日，新加坡，隶属第 13 海军陆战队远征部队海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队 (VMM) 364（增援）的一名美国海军陆战队员正在准备一架 MV-22B 鱼鹰，以便在黄蜂级两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 上起飞。美国海军陆战队照片周五，两栖攻击舰马金岛号根据当地船舶观察员和 AIS 数据，两栖船坞运输舰 LHD-8（LHD-8）和两栖船坞运输舰 USS John P. Murtha（LPD-26）已驶入新加坡三巴旺。马金岛和约翰·P·穆萨号与两栖运输船坞舰安克雷奇号 (LPD-23) 和已上船的第 13 海军陆战队远征部队组成了马金岛两栖待命大队。安克雷奇仍停靠在日本横须贺司令舰队活动中心。 2026 年 11 月 14 日，美国海军水手长三等大副马修·普里米蒂沃（左）和水手长二等大副杰伦·斯罗克莫顿在新加坡海上抛锚期间将千斤顶杆固定在独立型濒海战斗舰塔尔萨号（LCS-16）上。美国海军照片濒海战斗舰塔尔萨号（LCS-16）驶入新加坡周六出发，周一出发。塔尔萨隶属于第七驱逐舰中队（DESRON），该中队部署在东南亚前沿，是东南亚行动区指定舰艇的主要战术和作战指挥官。
在菲律宾马尼拉，澳大利亚总理安东尼·艾博内塞于 2026 年 11 月 15 日在菲律宾马尼拉参观澳大利亚皇家海军舰队加油船 HMAS Stalwart (A304)。澳大利亚国防军照片 澳大利亚皇家海军舰队加油船 HMAS Stalwart (A304) 对马尼拉进行港口访问。周日，正在出席东南亚国家联盟（ASEAN）峰会的澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内斯（Anthony Albanese）访问了这艘船，会见了船员和在菲律宾的澳大利亚国防军人员。 Stalwart 正在进行区域部署。 2026 年 11 月 16 日，南海，美国海军燃气轮机系统技术员（机械）海员谢恩·文森特（来自肯塔基州）在南海将军区斑马训练期间，对阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰拉尔夫·约翰逊号 (DDG-114) 上的通道中的斑马配件进行注释。美国海军照片 驱逐舰拉尔夫·约翰逊号（DDG-114）于周日穿越吕宋海峡，截至周一正在南海作业。拉尔夫·约翰逊（Ralph Johnson）前沿部署并分配到日本基地的DESRON 15。在越南海防，法国海军护卫舰FS Vendémiaire（F734）周一与越南海岸警卫队8004号近海巡逻船进行了联合搜救演习。此次演习是在法国护卫舰于11月12日开始访问海防后离开海防之后进行的。 Vendémiaire 总部位于新喀里多尼亚努美阿。
在菲律宾海 中国人民解放军海军辽宁舰仍部署在菲律宾海。该打击群最后一次被目击是在10月份，包括航母辽宁号（16）、巡洋舰鞍山号（101）和无锡号（104）以及驱逐舰淮南号（123）。此后随行船只可能发生了变化。在釜山，韩国皇家海军近海巡逻舰 HMS Spey (P234) 于 2026 年 11 月 16 日抵达韩国釜山进行港口访问。英国皇家海军照片 英国皇家海军近海巡逻舰 HMS Spey (P234) 周一抵达釜山进行港口访问。斯佩号和姊妹舰添马舰 (P233) 正在前沿部署

US Marine Corps photo On Friday, amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island (LHD-8) and amphibious transport dock USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26) pulled into Sembawang, Singapore , according to local ship spotters and AIS data. Makin Island and John P. Murtha , with amphibious transport dock USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and the embarked 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, form the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group. Anchorage remains docked at Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka in Japan. U.S. Navy Boatswain’s Mate 3rd Class Matthew Primitivo (left) and Boatswain’s Mate 2nd Class Jaron Throckmorton attach the jack staff aboard the Independence-variant littoral combat ship USS Tulsa (LCS-16) during sea and anchor in Singapore, Nov. 14, 2026. US Navy photo Littoral Combat Ship USS Tulsa (LCS-16) pulled into Singapore on Saturday and departed on Monday . Tulsa is assigned to Destroyer Squadron (DESRON) 7, which is forward deployed in Southeast Asia and is the primary tactical and operational commander of assigned ships in the Southeast Asia area of operations. In Manila, Philippines Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese visits Royal Australian Navy fleet oiler HMAS Stalwart (A304) on Nov. 15, 2026, in Manila, Philippines. Australian Defense Force photo Royal Australian Navy fleet oiler HMAS Stalwart (A304) carried out a port visit to Manila. On Sunday , Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, who was in town for the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit, visited the ship to meet with the crew and Australian Defense Force personnel in the Philippines. Stalwart is conducting a regional presence deployment. In the South China Sea U.S. Navy Gas Turbine Systems Technician (Mechanical) Seaman Shane Vincent, from Kentucky, annotates zebra fittings in a passageway aboard Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Ralph Johnson (DDG-114) during general quarters zebra training in the South China Sea, Nov. 16, 2026. US Navy photo Destroyer USS Ralph Johnson (DDG-114) was operating in the South China Sea as of Monday , having transited the Luzon Strait on Sunday . Ralph Johnson forward-deployed and assigned to Japan based DESRON 15. In Haiphong, Vietnam French Navy frigate FS Vendémiaire (F734) on Monday conducted a joint search and rescue exercise with Vietnam Coast Guard offshore patrol vessel 8004. The exercise followed the French frigate’s departure from Haiphong after a port visit that began on Nov. 12 . Vendémiaire is based in Noumea, New Caledonia. In the Philippine Sea The People’s Liberation Army Navy Liaoning CSG remains deployed in the Philippine Sea. The strike group was last visually sighted in October and included aircraft carrier CNS Liaoning (16) cruisers CNS Anshan (101) and CNS Wuxi (104) and destroyer CNS Huainan (123). The accompanying ships may have since changed. In Busan, South Korea Royal Navy offshore patrol vessel HMS Spey (P234) arrived Nov. 16, 2026, in Busan, South Korea, for a port visit. Royal Navy photo Royal Navy offshore patrol vessel HMS Spey (P234) arrived on Monday in Busan for a port visit. Spey and sister ship HMS Tamar (P233) are forward deployed to the Indo-Pacific. Near Honshu, Japan Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force helicopter destroyer JS Ise (DDH-182) and Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri (F49) near Honshu, Japan, on Nov. 13, 2026. JMSDEF photo Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force helicopter destroyer JS Ise (DDH-182) and Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri (F49) conducted the Japan-India Maritime Exercise (JAIMEX) 26 in waters south of Honshu from Nov. 13 to Saturday . The two ships carried out tactical maneuvering, communication and crossdeck drills. Sahyadri is making its way home after participating in Exercise Malabar 2026, which ran from Nov 5-12 in the waters off Yokosuka. In the East China Sea Royal Canadian Navy frigate HMCS Regina (FFH334) on Nov. 15, 2026, in the East China Sea. Royal Canadian Navy photo Royal Canadian Navy frigate HMCS Regina (FFH334) carried out a passing exercise with Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri in the East China Sea on Sunday . Regina is on deployment under Operation Horizon, the Canadian Armed Forces forward presence deployment to the Indo-Pacific and Operation Neon, the country’s surveillance and monitoring operations on North Korean maritime sanctions violations. The Royal Canadian Navy frigate carried out Operation Neon from late September to early November . Frank Cable pulled into CFAY on Nov. 11 for a port visit. Amphibious transport dock USS Anchorage , which has been anchored offshore since Nov. 11, moved into CFAY following Frank Cable’s departure, according to local ship spotters . Royal Canadian Navy frigate HMCS Regina arrived in Yokosuka on Thursday for a port visit. Fast attack submarine USS Toledo (SSN-769) pulled into CFAY on Tuesday , according to local shipspotters. In the Miyako Strait PLAN destroyer CNS Qiqihar (121) and fleet oiler CNS Chaohu (890) on Nov. 16, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo PLAN destroyer CNS Qiqihar (121) and fleet oiler CNS Chaohu (890) were spotted Monday sailing north 60 kilometers – 37 miles – west of Kume Island, having previously transited between Okinawa and Miyako Island to exit the Philippine Sea. A JMSDF P-3C Orion Maritime Patrol Aircraft shadowed the PLAN ships. Japan’s Joint Staff Office (JSO) noted that Qiqihar has traveled back and forth in Japan’s southwest region since Oct. 17 when it transited the Osumi Strait to enter the Pacific Ocean and then returned to the East China Sea through the Miyako Strait on Nov. 1. On Nov. 2, the PLAN destroyer sailed through the Miyako Strait to enter the Philippine Sea and returned the same way back into the East China Sea on Nov. 4. On Nov. 12, Qiqihar again sailed through the Miyako Strait to enter the Philippine Sea. The JSO also noted that Chaohu sailed south through the Miyako Strait to enter the Philippine Sea on Nov. 2. In the East China Sea A Chinese Y-9 electronic intelligence aircraft on Nov. 16, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Monday, a Chinese Y-9 electronic intelligence aircraft flew in from China and conducted a patrol circuit across the East China Sea, covering an area extending from south of the Danjo Islands to northwest of the island of Amami Oshima before returning to China. In response, the Japan Air Self-Defense Force scrambled fighter aircraft from the Southwestern Air Defense Command and other units. A Chinese TB-001 reconnaissance/attack Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) on Nov. 19, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Thursday, a Chinese TB-001 reconnaissance/attack Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) flew in from China and over the East China Sea as far as the waters southwest of the Danjo Islands and proceeded southwest. The drone flew west of Okinawa before returning to China. The JASDF scrambled fighter aircraft from the Southwestern Air Defense Command in response. In the Sea of Japan A Russian Tu-95 bomber on Nov. 17, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo Russian aircraft violated Japanese territorial airspace on two occasions and prompted fighter aircraft scrambles as they entered the Air Defense Identification Zones (ADIZs) of Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Tuesday. The three countries initially did not provide specifics of the Russian aircraft but later released the flights were conducted by two Tu-95MS bombers and two IL-76 transports, which landed in Vietnam that same day. title: Populists vs. Protesters: Czechs Fight Over Public Broadcasters

content:
一年中的大部分时间里，莱特纳平原都没有什么可以为当地人或游客提供的东西。这是布拉格斯巴达足球场对面的一大片毫无特色的土地。表面交替出现灰尘和泥土；有一个巴士停车场，有时还有马戏团。但莱特纳偶尔会举办一些可以让捷克政坛发生倾斜的活动。有时有一点。有时很多。 1989 年 11 月 25 日星期六，大约 75 万人聚集在一起，要求结束捷克斯洛伐克的共产主义政权。第二天，许多人返回，并于 11 月 29 日星期三，议会废除了共产党在社会中的领导地位。这次不会再发生类似的事情，但 11 月 15 日星期日，莱特纳岛上大约有 40 万人参加了自天鹅绒革命以来布拉格最大规模的示威活动。从媒体平台俯瞰旗帜和面孔的海洋时，它看起来很大。数万人聚集在那里抗议政府计划取消每月 10 美元的许可费，该许可费为该国两家公共广播公司捷克电视台和捷克广播电台提供资金。这似乎不是一个令人愤慨的提议，但对许多捷克人来说，这加深了他们对亿万富翁总理安德烈·巴比什及其民粹主义联盟的不信任。这位总理多年来一直在法庭上与欧盟补贴欺诈指控作斗争，他不喜欢公共广播。

For much of the year, Letná Plain has nothing to offer either locals or tourists.  It’s a large, featureless patch of land opposite the Sparta Prague football stadium. The surface alternates between dust and mud; there’s a car park for buses, and sometimes a circus. But every so often, Letná hosts an event that can tilt the world of Czech politics on its axis. Sometimes a little. Sometimes a lot.  On Saturday, November 25, 1989, around 750,000 people gathered to demand the end of Czechoslovakia’s communist regime. The following day, many returned, and on Wednesday, November 29, parliament abolished the Communist Party’s leading role in society. Nothing like that is going to happen this time around, but on Sunday, November 15, there were perhaps 400,000 people on Letná for the largest demonstration in Prague since the Velvet Revolution. It looked huge when viewed from a media platform overlooking an ocean of flags and faces.   The people who had gathered in the tens of thousands were there to protest against government plans to scrap the $10 monthly license fee which funds the nation’s two public broadcasters, Czech TV and Czech Radio. This may not seem an outrageous proposal, but to many Czechs it deepens their distrust of their billionaire Prime Minister Andrej Babiš and his populist coalition.   The premier, who has spent years in court fighting EU subsidy fraud allegations , is no fan of public broadcasting.  Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. In 2017, Babiš, who was then finance minister, described Czech TV’s investigative reporters as “a corrupt rabble making reports to order.” In 2024, he said public broadcasters were part of the then governing coalition’s “media division.”  But it is his coalition ally, the far-right SPD party, that has spearheaded the campaign to scrap the license fees and replace them with direct state funding. The fear is that state funds will come with strings pulled by politicians. Tokyo-born businessman Tomio Okamura, the SPD chairman and now parliament’s speaker, has said he would vote for a bill to abolish the broadcasters altogether if someone submitted one.  The third coalition partner is the MAGA-friendly Motorists for Themselves party, which was against scrapping the fees but is now in favor. One Motorist MP said public broadcasting had been turned into a totem by one half of Czech society, which was giving the other half the finger.  What is clear is that the government has not covered itself in glory. After months of vague and occasionally rancorous debate, and just days after all three coalition parties did poorly in Senate and local elections, the first reading of the bill was rushed through parliament in the middle of the night, with a vote scheduled for 4:36 am on Saturday, October 24. The bill envisages a cut in funding of around 15%, reversing an increase introduced by the previous government. Babiš is also floating alternative funding mechanisms, including voluntary contributions, and insists the government will not interfere in editorial decisions.  But there is a glaring contradiction. His government’s own impact assessment identifies the license fee as the funding mechanism that carries the smallest risk to the broadcasters’ independence. Direct state funding, it says, carries the greatest risk.  There has been much talk of “the Nordic model,” without acknowledging that there is no single Nordic model. Finland and Sweden, for example, have dedicated levies collected through the tax system, but Babiš has ruled out a new tax.  Observers are more worried about “the Slovak model.” There, the license fee was abolished in 2023 with a solemn promise to ringfence funding for Slovak Radio and TV and preserve its independence.  The following year, the broadcaster was dissolved by Robert Fico’s populist nationalist government and replaced. Critics say its successor is now toeing the government line. Babiš said he would not be deterred by mass demonstrations, though there was a tiny wobble from Culture Minister Oto Klempíř, who said after talks with Michael McGrath, the European Commissioner for Democracy and Justice, that he wanted to delay further debate on the bill until parliament had begun discussing legislation to implement the European Media Freedom Act.  The 72-year-old prime minister is in a tough spot. He seems tired and barely invested in the issue while his far-right coalition partner insists the fee has to go. Babiš is known to dislike big demonstrations, and the opposition senses an opportunity.  Following Klempíř’s suggestion to kick the issue into the long grass would be a logical course of action for the prime minister, but it may not be one that’s open to him.  Rob Cameron is a Prague-based journalist and broadcaster, and author of https://www.basedinbohemia.com/ where he writes about Central Europe through reporting, analysis and long-form storytelling. title: The military lacks an ‘overarching plan’ to improve munition stockpiles—partly because it’s no one’s job
zh_title: 军方缺乏改善弹药库存的“总体计划”——部分原因是这不是任何人的工作
summary: 根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军队可以购买的东西和实际需要的东西之间的差异。
content:
根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军方可以购买的东西与实际需要的东西之间存在差异，政府问责局表示，这甚至可能导致弹药投资超出五角大楼的要求。该报告的作者写道：“虽然国防部正在采取措施关注弹药短缺问题，但它无法解决这些差距。” “国防部没有总体计划，也没有指定和授权的领导层来改善弹药库存并满足其弹药需求。由于没有确定长期目标、实现这些目标的战略以及衡量进展的指标，国防部无法确定其行动是否能够解决弹药短缺问题。”包括国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在内的高级政府官员否认美国存在弹药短缺，尽管有报告和独立分析显示，伊朗冲突已经严重耗尽了弹药。关键武器，特别是备受追捧的爱国者拦截机，其制造时间可能超过两年。
但在对政府问责局研究的回应中，五角大楼官员同意军方需要制定一项长期计划来提高弹药生产的建议。五角大楼负责采购的代理副手大卫·卡德曼写道：“我们同意需要一个总体框架，更好地整合弹药需求、库存水平、生产、资源和长期目标。”他补充说，国防部“已经执行了政府问责局建议中的许多内容”。美国政府问责局的研究并未探讨特定弹药的库存，而是研究了五角大楼跟踪、预测和总体处理一系列武器（从炮弹到战斧导弹）的过程。 “重要的是，[这项研究]与当前的短缺无关，”战略与国际研究中心的高级顾问马克·坎西恩（Mark Cancian）撰写了大量有关弹药政策的文章。 “这关系到未来并决定长期库存、生产和弹药组合。”  国防官员强调需要“高低”弹药组合，即高科技、难以制造的武器和廉价武器之间的平衡。伊朗战争说明了美军对昂贵拦截机的依赖，这些拦截机投入了大量资金来击落廉价的沙赫德无人机，这些无人机的成本只有数万美元。
彭博资讯国防分析师韦恩·桑德斯表示：“当你拥有先进的能力，并且开始消耗先进的能力来击落快速补充的非先进能力时，这是一场我们赢不了的经济游戏。”“这开始转变为军事领域的一场革命，表明我们必须改变我们的学说，同时改变我们在美国的生产能力。”   美国政府问责局国防能力主管戴安娜·摩尔达夫斯基 (Diana Moldafsky) 在周五发给《防务一号》的一封电子邮件中指出，五角大楼已经发现了不足之处

【原文 English Original】
The Defense Department has no “overarching plan” to identify, achieve, or measure its progress toward long-term munition production goals, according to a Government Accountability Office study released on Thursday, which said the military was too reactive to global events and unprepared to forecast its own needs. The GAO cited—among other issues—a lack of centralized authority over weapons inventories, which have been depleted by the Iran war and are vital to U.S. plans for a potential conflict with China. At the center of the problem lies a discrepancy between what the military can buy and what it actually needs, which the GAO said could even result in munition investments that exceed the Pentagon’s requirements.  “While DOD is taking steps to focus on munitions shortages, it is not positioned to address these gaps,” the report’s authors wrote. “DOD does not have an overarching plan or designated and empowered leadership to improve munition inventories and meet its munitions requirements. By not identifying long-term goals, strategies to achieve them, and metrics to gauge progress, DOD cannot be sure that its actions will address its munition shortfalls. ” Top administration officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have denied that the U.S. has a shortage in munitions, despite reports and independent analyses showing the Iran conflict has alarmingly drained key weapons, especially for highly-sought Patriot interceptors that can take more than two years to make. But in its response to the GAO study, Pentagon officials concurred with the recommendation that the military needed to develop a long-term plan to improve its munition production.  “We agree with the need for an overarching framework that better integrates munition requirements, inventory levels, production, resources, and long-term objectives,” wrote David Cadman, the Pentagon’s acting deputy for acquisitions, who added that the department “already executes many elements” of the GAO’s recommendation. The GAO study did not explore the inventories of specific munitions, but examined the processes by which an expansive list of weapons — from artillery shells to Tomahawk missiles — are tracked, forecast and generally addressed by the Pentagon. “The important thing is that [the study] is not about current shortages,” Mark Cancian, a senior adviser with the Center for Strategic and International Studies who has written extensively on munitions policy. “It's about the future and deciding long-term inventories, production, and munitions mixes.”  Defense officials have emphasized the need for a “high-low” mix of munitions—that is, a balance between high-tech, hard-to-make weapons and cheaper ones. The Iran war illustrated the U.S. military’s reliance on expensive interceptors, which were heavily expended to shoot down cheap Shahed drones that only cost tens of thousands of dollars.  “When you have an exquisite capacity, and you are starting to expend an exquisite capacity to knock down non-exquisite capabilities that are rapidly replenished, it is an economical game that we're not going to win,” said Wayne Sanders, a defense analyst with Bloomberg Intelligence. “This is starting to turn into one of those revolutions in military affairs to say we have to change our doctrine as well as we change our production capacity in the U.S.”   In an email to Defense One on Friday, the GAO’s director for defense capabilities, Diana Moldafsky, noted that the Pentagon had identified shortfalls before the conflict with Iran, but said that the war “made addressing those shortages more urgent.” “Our key point is that meeting DOD's munitions requirements will be challenging,” Moldafsky said. “A department-wide plan would help the department direct its resources towards its most critical munitions needs.”  Cancian said that Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the consequent transfer of Patriots and other weapons to Kyiv, introduced concerns about the defense industrial base and its ability to respond to munition needs around the world. Meanwhile, the Pentagon has inked billions of dollars in multi-year “framework agreements” with top defense companies over the last year to help increase high-tech munition production, which require funding from Congress to come to fruition. The Trump administration also invoked the Defense Production Act earlier this year in an attempt to bolster munition supply chains. A Pentagon spokesperson declined to address the GAO study directly, or even to be quoted by name. But they said the military is “fully equipped to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing…while preserving a deep, ready stockpile to defend our people and interests.” Part of the problem is that no one authority is really in charge of keeping arsenals topped off and ready, the report found.  The GAO identified several Pentagon offices and working groups, including individual service entities, responsible for managing munition inventories, but no one dedicated authority “that empowers the leadership to make decisions that improve munitions inventories department-wide and hold them accountable for the outcomes achieved, such as improving munitions inventory levels.” The study also said that the services maintain separate tools to track munition inventories, which then feed into a Pentagon system known as the Munitions Readiness Initiative. But researchers said the DOD has limited oversight over that tracking platform and hasn’t regularly reconciled it with service-level numbers. Citing an unnamed Pentagon official in its acquisitions and sustainment office, the GAO said “the office was reluctant to impose additional responsibilities on the services for maintaining data to meet MRI’s needs because they recognize that the services already face numerous responsibilities in managing their own munitions inventory data.” The Pentagon concurred with most of the GAO’s recommendations, but only partially agreed with one: that the data management plan be run out of the DOD’s digital and AI office. Cadman’s response said that the Pentagon’s acquisition and sustainment arm was best suited to develop it. ]]>

title: Tai Po fire: Wang Fuk Court residents who sold titles excluded from third owners’ meeting next month
zh_title: 大埔火警：宏福苑卖业居民下月第三次业主大会被排除
summary: 政府指定的遭受火灾的宏福苑管理员已宣布下个月举行第三次业主会议，但已出售业权的居民除外。 2026 年 8 月 20 日，宏福苑周边地区仍被警方封锁。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。合安管理公司周一宣布，宏福苑自去年11月致命大火以来的第三次业主大会将于12月6日在大埔社区中心举行。这场大火造成 168 人死亡，数千人流离失所，成为香港数十年来最致命的火灾之一。与过去两次见面不同
content:
政府指定的遭受火灾的宏福苑管理员已宣布下个月举行第三次业主会议，但已出售业权的居民除外。 2026 年 8 月 20 日，宏福苑周边地区仍被警方封锁。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。合安管理公司周一宣布，宏福苑自去年11月致命大火以来的第三次业主大会将于12月6日在大埔社区中心举行。这场大火造成 168 人死亡，数千人流离失所，成为香港数十年来最致命的火灾之一。与过去的两次会议不同的是，下个月的会议将在一个地点举行，这表明合安预计出席人数将会减少。过去两次会议是在四个场地进行转播，以容纳大量前宏福苑居民。消息公布后，一些根据政府回购计划出售公寓的居民被告知，他们将不再有资格参加业主会议。 HKFP看到，在通过在线系统发出的通知中，Hop On表示，未在土地注册处记录中列为公寓注册业主的居民将无法报名参加下个月的会议。政府表示，宏福苑共有1,984户业主，其中99.3%表示愿意根据回购计划出售业权，只有13户拒绝出售。
当局表示，他们计划最早于明年立法收购所有未售出的业权。2026 年 7 月 19 日，宏福苑居民参加在大埔社区中心举行的业主会议。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。居民正在签署正式销售协议，将其产权转让给政府，一些居民已经开始根据换屋安排选择新的政府补贴单位。但据一位吴姓居民表示，一些尚未正式转让产权的居民或许可以参加下个月的会议。吴周一告诉《香港新闻社》，她的家人原计划在本月底签署正式合同，但现在要等到下个月的会议之后。合安表示，会议议程将包括宏福苑财务状况报告、任命2026财年审计师的决定，以及可能出现的任何其他事务。

【原文 English Original】
The government-appointed administrator of fire-hit Wang Fuk Court has announced a third owners’ meeting next month, excluding residents who have sold their titles. The area surrounding Wang Fuk Court remains blocked by police force on August 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Hop On Management announced on Monday that the third Wang Fuk Court owners’ meeting since last November’s deadly blaze will be held on December 6 at the Tai Po Community Centre. The blaze killed 168 people and displaced thousands, making it one of Hong Kong’s deadliest fires in decades. In a departure from the past two meetings — which were broadcast across four venues to accommodate a large turnout of former Wang Fuk Court residents — next month’s meeting will take place at a single venue, signalling that Hop On anticipates lower attendance. Following the announcement, some residents who had sold their flats under a government buyback scheme were told they would no longer be eligible to attend the owners’ meeting. In a notice issued via an online system and seen by HKFP, Hop On said residents not listed as a flat’s registered owner in Land Registry records would be unable to sign up for next month’s meeting. The government has said 99.3 per cent of all 1,984 Wang Fuk Court homeowners have indicated they are willing to sell their titles under the buyback scheme, leaving only 13 households refusing to sell. Authorities have said they plan to introduce legislation as early as next year to acquire any unsold titles. Wang Fuk Court residents attend a flat owners meeting at Tai Po Community Centre on July 19, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Residents are in the process of signing formal sales agreements to transfer their titles to the government, and some have begun selecting new government-subsidised units under a flat-swap arrangement. But some residents who have yet to formalise their title transfer may be able to attend next month’s meeting, according to one resident surnamed Woo. Woo told HKFP on Monday that her family had planned to sign the formal contract at the end of this month, but would now wait until after next month’s meeting. Hop On said the meeting agenda will include a report on Wang Fuk Court’s financial status, a decision on the appointment of an auditor for the 2026 financial year, and any other business that may arise.

title: Hong Kong to impose citywide drone ban, harbour and road curbs for Interpol General Assembly next week
zh_title: 香港下周将在国际刑警组织大会上实施全市无人机禁令、港口和道路限制
summary: 香港将在下周主办国际刑警组织年度峰会时实施空中、海上和陆地限制，限制无人机和小型飞机的行动以及维多利亚港部分地区的海上交通。当局将于 2026 年 11 月 30 日至 12 月 3 日第 94 届国际刑警组织大会期间在整个香港空域设立临时飞行限制区。图片：截图来自香港警方。国际刑警组织第94届大会将于11月30日至12月3日在香港举行，与会代表
content:
香港将在下周主办国际刑警组织年度峰会时实施空中、海上和陆地限制，限制无人机和小型飞机的行动以及维多利亚港部分地区的海上交通。当局将于 2026 年 11 月 30 日至 12 月 3 日第 94 届国际刑警组织大会期间在整个香港空域设立临时飞行限制区。图片：截图来自香港警方。国际刑警组织第94届大会将于11月30日至12月3日在香港举行，来自196个成员国的代表将出席，探讨全球安全问题。警方行动组总警司黄志荣在周一的新闻发布会上表示，预计将有超过 1000 人参加此次活动，其中包括国际刑警组织成员国的警察局长以及政府高级官员。他表示，峰会期间，香港的整个空域将被指定为临时飞行限制区，禁止无人机、小型飞机和直升机以及滑翔伞、风筝和“大量气球”进行未经授权的操作。黄用粤语说：“但这些限制不会影响民用飞机的运营。”他补充说，民航处将向航空公司和飞行员公布航空限制的范围。
他警告居民，在下周的临时禁令期间，不要在未经许可的情况下操作无人机，并指出，根据《小型无人机令》，违法者最高可被处以10万港元罚款和两年监禁。 海上和陆地交通限制 当局将限制国际刑警组织峰会将在湾仔举行的香港会议展览中心附近的维多利亚港部分地区的海上交通，同时会场周围的道路也将被关闭。 2024 年 4 月 3 日，一名男子俯瞰香港维多利亚港。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港水上的士是一条深受游客欢迎的跨海路线，在峰会期间将跳过湾仔站。行人也将被禁止进入会展中心外的长廊。黄先生呼吁居民留意交通管制，提前计划出行。他还敦促船只和巴士运营商提前计划，避免在国际刑警组织峰会场地附近接送乘客。黄补充说，警方将在活动期间协调港口和会场附近的海上和陆地交通。这是香港首次主办国际刑警组织大会，也是该活动第三次在中国举办。北京分别于1995年和2017年举办过两次。
上周，香港警方在邻近的中国城市深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织峰会期间逮捕了五名非法无人机操作男子，此前当局在香港北部领空的大部分地区实施了为期四天的禁飞区。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong will enforce air, sea and land restrictions when it hosts Interpol’s annual summit next week, limiting drone and small-aircraft operations as well as marine traffic in parts of Victoria Harbour. Authorities will impose a temporary restricted flying zone across the entire Hong Kong airspace for the duration of the 94th Interpol General Assembly from November 30 to December 3, 2026. Photo: Screenshot, via Hong Kong Police. The 94th International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) General Assembly is set to take place in Hong Kong from November 30 to December 3, with representatives from 196 member countries expected to attend to address global security issues. Wong Chi-wing, chief superintendent of the police’s operations wing, told a press conference on Monday that more than 1,000 people are expected to attend the event, including the police chiefs of Interpol’s member countries as well as senior government officials. He said Hong Kong’s entire airspace would be designated a temporary restricted flying zone for the duration of the summit, barring unauthorised operations of drones, small aircraft and helicopters, as well as paragliders, kites and “large numbers of balloons.” “But the restrictions will not affect civil aircraft operations,” Wong said in Cantonese, adding that the Civil Aviation Department would publicise the scope of the air restrictions for airlines and pilots. He warned residents against operating drones without a permit during the temporary ban next week, noting that offenders face a maximum penalty of a HK$100,000 fine and two years’ imprisonment under the Small Unmanned Aircraft Order. Sea and land traffic curbs Authorities will restrict marine traffic in parts of Victoria Harbour off the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai, where the Interpol summit will take place, while roads surrounding the venue will also be closed. A man looks out over Victoria Harbour in Hong Kong, on April 3, 2024. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The Hong Kong Water Taxi, a cross-harbour route popular with tourists, will skip its Wan Chai stop for the duration of the summit. Pedestrians will also be barred from entering the promenade outside the convention and exhibition centre. Wong urged residents to take note of the traffic restrictions and plan their journeys in advance. He also urged boat and bus operators to plan ahead and avoid picking up or dropping off passengers near the Interpol summit venue. Police will coordinate sea and land traffic in the harbour and near the venue for the duration of the event, Wong added. This will be the first time Hong Kong hosts the Interpol General Assembly and the third time the event has taken place in China. Beijing hosted it twice, in 1995 and 2017. Last week, Hong Kong police arrested five men over illegal drone operations during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the neighbouring Chinese city of Shenzhen, after authorities imposed a four-day restricted flying zone across much of Hong Kong’s northern airspace.

title: China’s Naval Developments Set For The Spotlight At Zhuhai Airshow
zh_title: 中国海军发展成为珠海航展的焦点
summary: 中国人民解放军海军表示，正在准备在即将于珠海举行的第十六届中国国际航空航天博览会上进行重要亮相，军舰、舰载机、先进武器系统和无人平台将成为重点展示。扩大后的海军部分将包括在海湾另一边的高栏港设立一个新的海事装备展区，这标志着解放军海军首次在此次活动中设立这样的专门展示区。珠海已成为国际防务、航空领域最重要的赛事之一
content:
中国人民解放军海军表示，正在准备在即将于珠海举行的第十六届中国国际航空航天博览会上进行重要亮相，军舰、舰载机、先进武器系统和无人平台将成为重点展示。扩大后的海军部分将包括在海湾另一边的高栏港设立一个新的海事装备展区，这标志着解放军海军首次在此次活动中设立这样的专门展示区。珠海已成为国际国防和航空航天史上最重要的活动之一，成为中国快速发展的航空和军事工业的主要公开展示地。两年一度的中国国际航空航天展览会（俗称中国航展）于 1996 年首次举办，为展示中国一些最先进的军事硬件提供了难得的机会，其中包括在其他地方很少如此详细展示的飞机和系统。虽然该活动也是中国航空航天工业向潜在国际客户推广其产品的主要平台，但它日益成为展示新军事能力和提供难以评估的项目的重要场所。
第十五届中国国际航空航天展览会（又称 2024 年中国航展）于 2024 年 11 月 15 日在中国广东省珠海市中国国际航空航天展览中心举行。摄影：VCG/VCG via Getty Images 前几届已经取得了一些特别重大的进展。 2016 年的展会上，J-20 隐形战斗机首次公开飞行亮相，而 2018 年的展会则以不同寻常的方式展示了这架飞机，包括展示其装载空对空导弹的内部武器舱。 2022年的展会上，歼20首次在珠海进行静态展示，同时还有运20重型运输机、直20直升机以及在展会上进行首次飞行演示的运20空中加油机。最近，2024 年的展会特别引人注目的是 J-35A 隐形战斗机的公开亮相和具有弹射能力的 J-15T 舰​​载战斗机的出现。一架 J-15T 舰​​载战斗机在 2024 年中国航展上进行飞行表演。CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images 今年的展览定于 12 月 7 日至 13 日举行，除其他外，将展示中国海军的广泛能力，特别强调其舰载航空能力的快速发展，这一点我们过去已经详细讨论过。
预计将亮相的最引人注目的飞机包括 J-15T 舰载战斗机、作战型 J-35 隐形战斗机、KJ-600 舰载机载预警和控制 (AEW&C) 飞机、Z-20 直升机的几种海军型号，也许最重要的是新型 JL-15 舰载教练机，它是陆基 JL-10 的发展型。JL-15 舰载教练机的照片突出显示了制动钩和弹射器发射杆。虽然我们之前在珠海见过 J-15T，但如果它配备国产 WS-10H2 发动机，将会引起特别的兴趣。这样的配置将让人们更仔细地了解中国舰载侧卫衍生产品的最新演变

【原文 English Original】
China’s People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) says it’s preparing a major presence at the upcoming 16th China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition in Zhuhai, with warships , carrier-based aircraft , advanced weapons systems, and uncrewed platforms set to feature prominently. The expanded naval component will include a new maritime equipment exhibition area at Gaolan Port, located just on the other side of the bay, marking the first time the PLAN has established such a dedicated display at the event. Zhuhai has become one of the most important events on the international defence and aerospace calendar, serving as China’s principal public showcase for its rapidly developing aviation and military industries. First held in 1996, the biennial China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, commonly known as Airshow China, provides an unusual opportunity to see some of the country’s most advanced military hardware, including aircraft and systems that are rarely shown in such detail elsewhere. While the event also serves as a major platform for China’s aerospace industry to promote its products to potential international customers , it has increasingly become an important venue for revealing new military capabilities and offering glimpses of programs that are otherwise difficult to assess. A general view of the 15th China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, or Airshow China 2024, at the China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition Center on November 15, 2024, in Zhuhai, Guangdong Province of China. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images Previous editions have produced some particularly significant developments. The 2016 show saw the J-20 stealth fighter make its first public flying appearance , while the 2018 edition provided an unusually revealing look at the aircraft, including a demonstration of its internal weapons bays, loaded with air-to-air missiles . The 2022 exhibition featured the J-20 on static display for the first time at Zhuhai, alongside the Y-20 heavy transport aircraft, Z-20 helicopter, and YY-20 aerial refueling tanker, which made its first flying demonstration at the event. More recently, the 2024 exhibition was particularly notable for the public debut of the J-35A stealth fighter and the appearance of the catapult-capable J-15T carrier-based fighter. A J-15T carrier-based fighter conducts a flight demonstration at Airshow China 2024. CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images This year’s exhibition, scheduled to take place from December 7 to 13, will showcase, among others, a broad range of the PLAN’s capabilities, with a particularly notable emphasis on the rapid evolution of its carrier aviation capabilities, something we have addressed in detail in the past . Among the most noteworthy aircraft expected to feature are the J-15T carrier-based fighter, the operational J-35 stealth fighter, the KJ-600 carrier-based airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft, several naval variants of the Z-20 helicopter, and, perhaps most significantly, the new JL-15 carrier-capable trainer, a development of the land-based JL-10 . A photo of the JL-15 carrier-capable trainer with the arrestor hook and catapult launch bar highlighted. Chinese internet via X While we have seen the J-15T at Zhuhai before, the aircraft will be of particular interest if it is shown with the indigenous WS-10H2 engine. Such a configuration would offer a closer look at the latest evolution of China’s carrier-based Flanker derivative and its ongoing transition toward a more domestically supported carrier aviation ecosystem. The appearance of the J-35 would be another major highlight. The aircraft represents a significant step in the PLAN’s carrier aviation ambitions, bringing a fifth-generation stealth fighter capability into the carrier air wing. Its presence would provide another opportunity to examine the progress of China’s next-generation naval fighter program. Back in 2014, Zhuhai saw the public debut of the FC-31 fighter demonstrator. At the time, it was still a land-based concept, and export was the main talking point, although there was already speculation about a naval variant, today’s J-35. A People’s Liberation Army Navy J-35 fighter during trials from the carrier Fujian last year. Chinese internet via X Meanwhile, the KJ-600 is arguably one of the most important developments in the PLAN’s carrier aviation ecosystem. The twin-engine turboprop aircraft is designed to provide airborne early warning and battle management capabilities, something that would transform the situational awareness and coordination available to China’s carrier strike groups. One of the first high-definition photos of the KJ-600 carrier-based airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft. Chinese internet via X Several variants of the Z-20 family are also expected to feature, reflecting the growing importance of helicopters in carrier operations, including airborne anti-submarine warfare, utility, and other maritime support missions. You can read more about the Z-20 family and other Chinese rotary-wing developments in this previous TWZ deep-dive on the topic . A Z-20F, the anti-submarine warfare variant of the naval Z-20 family. Three more naval Z-20s are seen in the hangar behind, including a Z-20J shipborne transport and assault variant. Chinese internet via X Perhaps the most intriguing aircraft on the list, however, is the JL-15. The JL-15 is derived from the Hongdu JL-10, also exported as the L-15 Falcon, a twin-engine advanced jet trainer and lead-in fighter trainer. The navalized development was initially reported to be designated JL-10J, but is now confirmed as being the JL-15. A tailhook-equipped mockup was spotted alongside the aircraft carrier Fujian in 2024. However, its operational status remains unclear, and China is known to have encountered difficulties with its earlier JL-9G naval trainer, whose tailhook was reportedly deleted following structural problems. Regarding the rumoured JL-10J carrier-capable jet trainer, another hint was spotted next to the carrier Fujian: It appears to be an unfinished JL-10J mockup stored on the dockside . So question is: Two tails as shown in the latest CG or just one like the regular JL-10? pic.twitter.com/BM8W8MRGWK — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) March 19, 2024 Its appearance would provide a particularly interesting indication of how China is thinking about training its next generation of carrier-based pilots. A carrier-capable development of the JL-10 would be an important addition to the emerging carrier aviation ecosystem, bridging the gap between conventional jet training and the demanding requirements of operating from an aircraft carrier. The JL-15 also makes an interesting comparison with the U.S. Navy’s somewhat stuttering efforts to introduce a new training jet for its carrier pilots. The U.S. Navy’s Undergraduate Jet Training System (UJTS) program is intended to replace its aging fleet of T-45 Goshawk trainers, but the acquisition effort has encountered considerable difficulties. Earlier this month, we described how Sierra Nevada Corporation (SNC) withdrew its proposed clean-sheet Freedom Jet from the competition, citing concerns over the Navy’s insistence on firm-fixed-price production commitments before the aircraft’s design had sufficiently matured. This leaves the Beechcraft M-346N , based on Leonardo’s established M-346 Master , as the only publicly known remaining contender . The program has also experienced schedule slippage, with the initial contract award now expected in the fourth quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. Perhaps more significant is the difference in the two services’ approaches to carrier aviation training. The U.S. Navy has removed the requirement for its next-generation jet trainer to be capable of operating from an actual aircraft carrier, including carrier qualification and simulated carrier touch-and-goes at land-based facilities. Instead, it increasingly relies on advanced simulation, virtualized training, and assisted carrier landing technologies to prepare pilots for the demands of carrier operations. The JL-15, by contrast, is intended to support carrier-based pilot training. A dedicated carrier-capable trainer could offer China a more direct pathway for preparing pilots for operations aboard its increasingly sophisticated — and expanding — carrier fleet. Taken together, the PLAN aircraft being lined up for Zhuhai this year illustrate the increasingly sophisticated and integrated nature of China’s carrier aviation ambitions . As well as the aircraft carriers and their embarked aircraft, these ambitions also require other surface and subsurface vessels to operate effectively. Uncrewed systems will form another important part of the display. The exhibition will include aerial drones, uncrewed underwater vehicles, and other autonomous platforms, reflecting the PLAN’s growing interest in the potential of uncrewed warfare. Chinese media reports suggest that the WZ-2 uncrewed helicopter will receive its public debut at Zhuhai, while the PLAN may well also want to capitalize on its recent announcement that it had successfully launched and recovered a GJ-21 stealthy flying-wing uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV) aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . GJ-21. Chinese internet via X A chance to see the GJ-21 up close would be a huge deal, but there are many other naval drone options that could be revealed in more detail. There are likely to be more navalized collaborative combat aircraft (CCA) concepts and developments, especially since the adoption of the electromagnetic aircraft launch system (EMALS) catapult opens up a huge range of possibilities for uncrewed aircraft operating as part of a carrier air wing. Potentially, these could include the mysterious MQ-25-like drone that we recently discussed , the role of which remains unclear. On top of that, constant CCA testing at locations such as Malan suggests there could be much more to discuss than just the systems officially highlighted. Many other naval drones will surely be on display as well, including lower-end attritable concepts. Beyond static displays, China’s navy plans to organize flight demonstrations, formation flights, and simulated operational exercises. Its stated aim is to highlight not only the capabilities of individual platforms but also their ability to operate together in complex maritime environments. Photos have emerged showing apparent rehearsals for the display, presenting examples of the J-15, J-35, and KJ-600 to represent Beijing’s broader carrier air wing ecosystem. Two J-15s, two J-35s, and a KJ-600 purportedly taking part in a rehearsal for a formation fly-over at Zhuhai. Chinese internet via X It is not immediately clear which versions of the J-15 are participating in this formation flight: they could be J-15Ts, but another possibility is the electronic warfare version, the J-15DT , that we have profiled in the past. Regardless, they highlight how China’s carrier aviation ambitions are increasingly focused on catapult-assisted takeoff but arrested recovery (CATOBAR) operations, which offer many advantages . The J-15DT electronic warfare version of the Chinese carrier Flanker is outfitted for operations aboard catapult-equipped flattops like the Fujian . Chinese internet via X For the first time, the exhibition will also include a substantial surface fleet component, making use of the docks at the nearby Gaolan Port. Among the vessels expected to be featured are the Type 075 amphibious assault ship, the Type 055 guided-missile destroyer, and the Type 054A guided-missile frigate. Their presence will offer a public-facing showcase of China’s increasingly sophisticated surface fleet and its expanding range of maritime capabilities. It should also be recalled that it was at Gaolan Port where at least one Chinese uncrewed surface vessel , a distinctive trimaran craft, was first spotted. The Type 055 guided-missile destroyer Nanchang sails during the naval exercise Joint Sea-2021 on October 19, 2021, in the Western part of the Pacific Ocean. Photo by Sun Zifa/China News Service via Getty Images The broader messaging surrounding the exhibition is also notable. According to the PLAN, this year’s displays will place greater emphasis on operational readiness and training, with active-duty equipment that regularly participates in exercises and maritime security missions taking precedence over purely exhibition-oriented displays. This should underscore how Beijing has rapidly spun up its naval capabilities, introducing new and more capable equipment that is increasingly capable of more sustained out-of-area operations. The expanded naval presence at Zhuhai looks set to provide a substantial public showcase of China’s ongoing naval modernization. As well as the combination of the J-15T, J-35, KJ-600, and Z-20 variants, the JL-15 points to an increasingly comprehensive carrier aviation enterprise. And, judging by previous editions of the show, there will almost certainly be more novelties on display as well. Murtha (LPD-26) 和登船的第 13 海军陆战队远征部队。2026 年 11 月 8 日，在佛罗里达州梅波特，分配给自由型濒海战斗舰圣路易斯号 (LCS-19) 的一级消防员大卫·罗宾逊 (David Robinson) 在该船从大沼泽港出发时收起系泊缆。美国海军照片 濒海战斗舰 USS 明尼阿波利斯-圣保罗号(LCS-21) 和圣路易斯号 (LCS-19) 被分配给美国南方司令部，但目前停泊在佛罗里达州梅波特海军基地的港口。2026 年 11 月 13 日，土耳其海军 SH-70 直升机在地中海“马维·巴利纳”演习的摄影演习中编队飞过阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰布尔克利号 (DDG-84)。在地中海作战的独立部署的导弹驱逐舰包括：美国海军奥斯卡·奥斯汀号（DDG-79），母港为罗塔海军基地。 USS Bulkeley (DDG-84)，母港为罗塔海军基地。 2026 年 11 月 21 日，红海，一名水手在阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰“冈萨雷斯”号 (DDG-66) 上夜间使用六分仪观测月亮。美国海军照片 有两艘导弹驱逐舰在红海作业：“杰森·邓纳姆”号 (DDG-109)，母港为佛罗里达州梅波特海军基地。“冈萨雷斯”号 (DDG-66)，母港位于弗吉尼亚州诺福克海军基地。在阿拉伯海，一名水手观察刘易斯和克拉克级干货船美国海军塞萨尔·查韦斯号 (T-AKE-14) 与尼米兹级航空母舰乔治·H·W·布什号并肩航行。
