The United States International Trade Commission.
Request for comments regarding International Trade Commission's Economic Analysis, Investigation No. MISC-054.
Pursuant to Section 332 of the Tariff Act of 1930, the United States International Trade Commission (Commission) is seeking information from the public on its economic analysis, including its methodology and areas of focus.
To ensure consideration, written comments must be submitted on or before March 25, 2027.
Lisa R. Barton, Secretary to the Commission, U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Washington, DC 20436, telephone 202-205-2595. General information concerning the Commission may be obtained by accessing its internet server at https://www.usitc.gov. Hearing-impaired persons are advised that information can be obtained by contacting the Commission's TDD terminal on (202) 205-1810.
You may submit comments, identified by docket number MISC-054, by any of the following methods:
Agency Website: https://www.usitc.gov. You may submit comments on the Commission's electronic docket (EDIS) at https://edis.usitc.gov. For help accessing EDIS, please email EDIS3Help@usitc.gov.
Email: Submit comments via to Secretary@usitc.gov. Include docket ( printed page 76266) number MISC-054 in the subject line of the message. Comments submitted by email must be: in letter format and double-spaced (unless the document is less than two (2) pages); in portable document format (PDF); and signed with either a typed or written signature. All comments received will be posted without change to the agency's public record, including any personal information provided.
Instructions: All submissions received must include the agency name and docket number (MISC-054, along with written comments addressing the topics on which the USITC seeks information. All comments received will be posted without change to https://www.usitc.gov, including any personal information provided. Written comments filed on EDIS must conform to the provisions of section 201.8 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR 201.8).
Docket: For access to the docket to read background documents or comments received, go to https://www.usitc.gov and/or the U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Room 112, Washington, DC 20436.
Jennifer Andberg, Office of External Relations ((202) 205-3404, or Jennifer.Andberg@usitc.gov). Hearing-impaired individuals may obtain information on this matter by contacting the Commission's TDD terminal at 202-205-1810. General information about the Commission is available by accessing the Commission website at www.usitc.gov. Persons with mobility impairments who will need special assistance in gaining access to the Commission should contact the Office of the Secretary at (202) 205-2000.
1. Relevant Statutory Authorities
Pursuant to section 332 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1332 (“section 332”)), whenever requested, the Commission submits to the President, and, by delegation, the United States Trade Representative (USTR); the Senate Finance Committee (SFC); or the House Ways and Means Committee (HWM) information and analysis on any matter related to tariffs, international trade, and industry competitiveness. Additionally, the President or Congress can task the Commission with factfinding investigations on various topics, which the Commission can also institute on its own initiative. Other statutes such as section 131 of the Trade Act of 1974 and statutes for specific trade agreements also provide authority to conduct factfinding investigations.
The Commission's work under section 332 and these other authorities utilize some degree of economic analysis. In such investigations, the Commission often analyzes the ways that trade and trade policy affect U.S. workers, producers, consumers, and the U.S. economy as a whole. The analysis helps inform policymakers' decisions on trade policy and international trade negotiations. In conjunction with other factfinding tools such as public hearings and written submissions, the Commission often uses analytical approaches including quantitative models, which are simplified, mathematical representations of an economy or industry using certain real-world data, to help isolate—and thereby understand—the impact of a past or future change when many factors could affect the outcomes.
To ensure that the Commission can meet the challenges posed by changing global and economic circumstances that are highly relevant to trade, it has decided to evaluate on an ongoing basis its analytical tools, data sources, and methodologies to ensure its work remains accurate, relevant, and responsive to its stakeholders.
2. Commission Analytical Approaches and How They Are Used
Given the variety of topics the Commission is obligated to analyze, the Commission uses a variety of analytical techniques, which can be combined to suit the topic(s) to be examined, including qualitative analysis, quantitative analysis without modeling, and quantitative analysis with economic modeling, which, as mentioned, can help assess the impact of a policy change by filtering out other factors, with important caveats.
The Commission's models vary by technique and scope. Major simulation models are built at the level of an industry or the entire economy. At the economy-wide level, the main modeling approach at the Commission has historically been the computable general equilibrium (CGE) model, based on the Global Trade Analysis Project (GTAP) database. This approach has been deployed numerous times in both factfinding investigations, such as in the evaluation of the likely impact of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) that the Commission published in 2019 (Inv. No. TPA-105-003, U.S.-Mexico-Canada Trade Agreement: Likely Impact on the U.S. Economy and on Specific Industry Sectors). Meanwhile, industry-level partial equilibrium models focus on a single economic sector without modeling the interactions between economic sectors, such as in the Commission's regular assessments of the USMCA automotive rules of origin (Inv. No. 332-600, USMCA Automotive Rules of Origin: Economic Impact and Operation, 2025 Report).
Although less frequently deployed in factfinding investigations as stand-alone models, econometric models have been used, for example, to measure the extent of “pass-through” from tariffs to U.S. prices in the Commission's analysis of the impact of the tariffs imposed in 2023 under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 and section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 (Inv. No. 332-591, Economic Impact of Section 232 and 301 Tariffs on U.S. Industries). More recently, in place of a CGE model, the Commission used an econometric “gravity” equation as part of a general equilibrium gravity model in a 2026 study on the impact of revoking China's permanent normal trade relations status (Inv. No. 330-609, Effects on the U.S. Economy of Revoking China's Permanent Normal Trade Relations Status).
In addition to the above trade models that have generally been focused on medium- and long-run outcomes, such as by assuming the entire U.S. labor force is employed and can move freely across sectors, the Commission is considering how to develop and deploy economic models that are more equipped to look at short-term outcomes before employment, wages and other aspects of the economy fully adjust to any policy change.
Because models cannot capture every feature of the real world, they necessarily rely on assumptions and simplifications. Different modeling approaches may also emphasize different channels through which policies affect economic outcomes. Economy-wide simulation models, such as CGE models, have been subject to criticism regarding certain assumptions, including assumptions about full employment and worker mobility across sectors, particularly when used to analyze the effects of trade policy changes.
II. Topics on Which USITC Seeks Information
The Commission seeks information from the public on any of the following topics. After the comment period concludes, the Commission intends to produce a report that includes a summary of comments. The comments will also inform how the Commission moves forward with its factfinding Section 332 and related responsibilities. ( printed page 76267)
1. Do you think the Commission currently has the right analytical tools, including economic models, to address major trade policy questions over the next 5-10 years? Why or why not?
a. What non-modeling approaches should the Commission's analytical toolkit include?
b. What is the full suite of models ( e.g., industry-specific versus economy-wide; short-term versus long-term) that the Commission should have available for use in its analysis?
2. What factors or topics should the Commission's economic analysis be able to consider? Would they include, but not be limited to, the following:
a. Effect of trade on labor markets
i. Short-term effect on workers
ii. Long-term effect on workers ( e.g., changes in workforce capacity or skill sets in certain industries)
iii. Effect on the quality of jobs available for workers, including any shifts in wages, benefits, or job security
b. Effect of trade on investment
c. Effect of hostile trade actions, including boycotts, export controls, or other trade sanctions placed on the United States or U.S. persons
d. Effect of trade on distribution of wealth/income within the United States, including across geographic regions and demographic groups
e. Effect of trade on the environment
f. Effect of trade on immigration
g. Interaction of trade policy with domestic policies and regulations ( e.g. intellectual property, environmental regulations, labor regulations, tax policy, immigration policy)
h. Interaction of trade with domestic and international protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights
i. Interaction with trade imbalances
j. Interaction with market concentration
k. Other topics you believe would be useful for the Commission to consider
3. Given the Commission's statutory obligations, which of the above topics should the Commission prioritize?
4. Please discuss what trade questions are well suited to modeling, and which are better served by a different sort of analysis, such as descriptive trend analysis, legal analysis, or other analytical approaches.
5. How effective have the Commission's models been at evaluating the effects of major trade policy changes in past years? Please reference specific examples.
6. How can the Commission best engage in quality control of its modeling prospectively and evaluate the accuracy of its modeling retrospectively? Should the Commission regularly and publicly undertake model validation to evaluate the accuracy of its models?
7. Are there existing alternatives to Commission models that are more accurate, or that would capture factors that the Commission should consider? What trade-offs, if any, might such other models have?
8. Are there other branches of economics or disciplines outside of economics that might be useful in helping the Commission improve its modeling and other analytical techniques? Please provide specific examples of techniques, papers, authors, or other details to help the Commission identify these items.
9. How can the Commission incorporate or improve any of the following practices, and are there examples of best practices from a Commission report or external report:
a. Sensitivity analysis to test the importance of assumptions on model outcomes
b. Indications as to the level of certainty of model estimates
c. Plain narrative explanation and data visualization
d. Transparency of model assumptions and limitations
e. Replicability of model releases
10. Should the Commission attempt to quantify the impact of nontariff measures (NTMs) on trade? If quantification is appropriate, how should this be conducted? How should the Commission account for the potential non-trade-related impacts of NTMs ( e.g., on public health and the environment)?
11. What datasets should be created, refined, or expanded upon for the Commission's use on understanding the effects of trade policy?
12. How can the Commission make the best use of AI tools for quantitative analysis?
13. Are there any ways in which the Commission's information-gathering techniques such as public hearings, field visits, written submission periods, or surveys can be improved?
14. From whom ( e.g., the public and/or technical experts) should the Commission receive input regarding its analytical approaches, and with what frequency and in what manner should the Commission solicit such input? Would the Commission benefit from establishing a public advisory council for economic modeling?
15. Anything else that the submitter believes would help the Commission improve its modeling.
III. Submission Instructions
Written submissions: Interested persons are invited to file written submissions and other information concerning the matters to be addressed in this request. All written submissions should be addressed to the Secretary, and should be received no later than 5:15 p.m., March 25, 2027. All written submissions must conform to the provisions of section 201.8 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR 201.8). Filings must be made through the Commission's Electronic Document Information System (EDIS, https://edis.usitc.gov) or via email. Persons with questions regarding electronic filing should contact the Office of the Secretary, Docket Services Division (202-205-1802), email EDIS3help@usitc.gov, or consult the Commission's Handbook on Filing Procedures.
Any submissions that contain confidential business information (CBI) must also conform with the requirements in section 201.6 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR 201.6). Section 201.6 of the rules requires that the cover of the document and the individual pages be clearly marked as to whether they are the “confidential” or “nonconfidential” version, and that the CBI is clearly identified by means of brackets. All written submissions, except for CBI, will be made available for inspection by interested persons.
All information, including CBI, submitted may be disclosed to and used: (i) by the Commission, its employees and Offices, and contract personnel (a) for developing or maintaining the records of this or a related proceeding, or (b) in internal investigations, audits, reviews, and evaluations relating to the programs, personnel, and operations of the Commission including under 5 U.S.C. Appendix 3; or (ii) by U.S. government employees and contract personnel for cybersecurity or other security purposes. The Commission will not otherwise disclose any CBI in a manner that would reveal the operations of the firm supplying the information.
By order of the Commission.
Issued: November 23, 2026.

腾讯和阿里巴巴等中国公司警告称，扩张计划将被推迟并可能被削减
中国正在加大自力更生力度，但国产芯片仍落后
新加坡/北京 — — 黄仁勋可能会重新执掌英伟达，但他的回归并没有给依赖美国先进芯片的中国人工智能公司带来什么喘息的机会。
分析人士表示，11 月 19 日生效的美国新规定使中国企业更难从海外数据中心租用计算能力，从而在短期内对中国人工智能的发展造成重大挫折。
但这些限制措施可能会给中国多年来推动技术自力更生的努力增添新的紧迫性，将企业曾经视为后备计划的开发本土芯片和计算系统变成优先事项。
中国的人工智能行业知道，它不能再依赖黄仁勋来帮助确保获得英伟达的先进芯片。 11 月 23 日恢复担任首席执行官的黄仁勋曾是华盛顿最强烈主张继续向中国销售芯片的人之一。
新加坡南洋理工大学经济学名誉教授陈光炎表示：“对中国来说，最重要的教训是，它不能依赖个别美国企业领导人的善意，无论他们的商业影响力或与中国接触的意愿如何。”
总部位于华盛顿的咨询公司亚洲集团 (The Asia Group) 负责数字业务的合伙人乔治·陈 (George Chen) 指出，英伟达董事会已经成立了一个新委员会，负责监督国家安全风险和出口管制合规情况。
“英伟达肯定会在合规方面加倍努力，因为它不想再次被指责与中国过于亲密，”陈告诉海峡时报。
美国商务部工业与安全局11月16日宣布的新规定禁止美国境外的数据中心为具有强大计算能力的中国客户提供服务，除非获得美国政府许可。
由于远程访问占中国公司人工智能计算能力的近三分之一，科技巨头已经警告称，美国的限制可能会扰乱他们的计划。
腾讯表示，先进计算能力的减少可能会延长开发下一代混元人工智能模型所需的时间。腾讯总裁刘炽平在 11 月 18 日的财报电话会议上表示：“这让中国的每个人都感到沮丧。”
一天后，阿里巴巴首席执行官埃迪·吴表示，该公司可能会缩减其长期数据中心扩张目标。
这种不确定性也影响到了贷方。银行家已暂停一项拟议的 4.8 亿美元（6.2 亿新元）贷款，该贷款旨在支付马来西亚数据中心的 Nvidia 芯片费用，该数据中心将为 TikTok 的中国所有者字节跳动提供服务。

【原文 English Original】
China’s AI chip crunch deepens after US curbs | The Straits Times
Jensen Huang is back, but China’s AI chip crunch is far from over
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
China’s AI industry knows it can no longer lean on Jensen Huang to help secure access to Nvidia’s advanced chips.
Published Nov 25, 2026, 09:40 PM
Updated Nov 25, 2026, 10:53 PM
New US rules will curb Chinese access to advanced chips and overseas data centres, likely slowing AI model development
Chinese firms such as Tencent and Alibaba warn of delays and possible cuts to expansion plans
China is pushing harder for self-reliance, but homegrown chips still lag behind
SINGAPORE/BEIJING – Jensen Huang may be back at the helm of Nvidia, but his return offers little reprieve to Chinese AI firms that rely on advanced US chips.
Analysts say new US rules, which took effect on Nov 19, deal a significant setback to China’s artificial intelligence development in the near term by making it harder for Chinese firms to rent computing power from overseas data centres.
But the curbs are likely to add fresh urgency to China’s years-long push for technological self-reliance, turning what firms once saw as a back-up plan – developing home-grown chips and computing systems – into a priority.
China’s AI industry knows it can no longer lean on Huang to help secure access to Nvidia’s advanced chips. Huang, who was reinstated as chief executive on Nov 23, was once one of the most vocal advocates in Washington of continued chip sales to China.
“The most important lesson for China is that it cannot depend on the goodwill of individual American corporate leaders, regardless of their commercial influence or willingness to engage with China,” said Tan Kong Yam, an emeritus professor of economics at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.
George Chen, a partner who leads digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy, noted that Nvidia’s board has set up a new committee to oversee national security risks and compliance with export controls.
“Nvidia will surely double down on compliance because it won’t want to be accused again of being too cosy with China,” Chen told The Straits Times.
The new rules announced by the US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security on Nov 16 prohibit data centres outside the US from serving Chinese clients with significant computing power, unless licensed by the US government.
With remote access accounting for nearly a third of AI computing power for Chinese firms, tech giants have already warned that the US curbs could disrupt their plans.
Tencent said reduced access to advanced computing power could lengthen the time it takes to develop a future generation of its Hunyuan AI model. “It sets everyone back in China,” said Tencent president Martin Lau on a Nov 18 earnings call.
A day later, Alibaba chief executive Eddie Wu said the company could scale back its long-term data centre expansion target.
The uncertainty has reached lenders too. Bankers have paused work on a proposed US$480 million (S$620 million) loan sought to pay for Nvidia chips at a Malaysian data centre that would serve ByteDance, the Chinese owner of TikTok.
Benjamin Ho, lead research strategist for Hong Kong and China equities at Maybank Investment Banking Group, notes how at least two of Nvidia’s server partners have suspended deliveries to customers in South-east Asia amid the new US curbs.
“I think model iteration and roll-outs will slow down significantly, and you will probably see this become more severe in the coming months,” he told ST.
Since Washington began restricting exports of advanced Nvidia chips to China in 2022, Chinese tech firms have increasingly rented computing power from overseas data centres.
Even before the November restrictions, Chinese companies were scrambling to secure overseas computing capacity, Reuters reported on Nov 12.
Overseas data centres supply roughly 30% of the AI computing power available to Chinese firms, estimates Sigrid Wang, lead technology analyst at Hutong Research, an independent Chinese advisory firm.
Before the Nov 16 curbs, the Washington-based Institute for Progress think-tank projected that the computing power Chinese firms could tap through overseas data centres would nearly triple, from the equivalent of about one million Nvidia H100 chips at the end of 2026 to 2.8 million a year later.
Ho of Maybank expects a fierce fight to ensue among Chinese AI companies for scarce domestic computing resources, noting how top Chinese chipmaker SMIC is already operating at 98% capacity and buyers like DeepSeek are facing wait times of more than a year for the latest chips.
In such a battle, Ho said tech giants like Baidu, Tencent and Alibaba are best positioned, thanks to early investments in domestic data centres and hardware. Pure AI start-ups like Moonshot AI and MiniMax, on the other hand, are the most vulnerable as they would need to rent computing capacity from their rivals.
In the AI race with the US, this is the one advantage China has
As US ups stakes on AI, can China win over the world with open-weight models?
Access to Nvidia chips inside China remains uncertain. Nvidia has confirmed it stopped shipping its H200 processors to China despite receiving some US export licences.
Beijing has also urged Chinese firms to use home-grown chips, and withheld approval for a shipment of about 600,000 H200s to enter from Hong Kong, according to a Nov 5 Reuters report.
“Were Nvidia to stop supplying China with its H20 and H200 chips altogether, Chinese chipmakers would have a huge gap to fill,” Hutong analyst Wang said, adding that Nvidia accounted for 55% of China’s AI chips market in 2025.
Chinese firms including Huawei, Baidu, Alibaba and Cambricon have made strides in designing AI processors, but China has limited capacity to manufacture them.
This manufacturing bottleneck could tighten further, said Guo Shan, a partner at Hutong, if the US Congress passes the MATCH Act. The Bill seeks to press allies such as the Netherlands and Japan to tighten controls on sales to China of the equipment used to make advanced chips.
While Huawei has built clusters known as supernodes that connect many chips at high speed, allowing them to train and run large AI models together, they remain prohibitively costly.
Wang said Huawei’s Cloudmatrix 384 can rival Nvidia’s GB200 NVL72 system on some measures, but its eye-popping price of US$8 million puts it out of reach for smaller Chinese AI developers.
Jensen Huang is back, but it won’t be business as usual for Taiwan’s tech industry
US chip curbs put South-east Asia’s data centre ambitions to the test
There is also a trade-off. Linking more processors can help close the performance gap, but it strains China’s already limited supply of home-grown chips.
A scholar who advises the Chinese government on AI policy acknowledged that his country’s chips and computing systems still lagged behind America’s, but remained optimistic about China’s long-term potential.
He spoke with ST on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the media.
“Instead of bemoaning how the US curbs will handicap us, we would rather see them as giving us a window period to grow ourselves,” he said.
Kok Yufeng is a China correspondent at The Straits Times based in Beijing.

summary: 中国在亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席 - 大西洋理事会中国 东亚 能源与环境 地缘政治与能源安全 2026 年 11 月 25 日 • 东部时间上午 10:04 中国在亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席 霍尔木兹海峡冲击发生九个月后，能源安全已被列入上周日本-东盟和亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会的议程。五年来的第二次价格冲击迫使亚洲政策制定者重新考虑能源安全规划和机构，但中国并没有带头，尽管它在地区能源领域发挥着重要作用。
content:
大西洋理事会：亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席中国
中国东亚 能源与环境 地缘政治与能源安全
2026 年 11 月 25 日 • 上午 10:04（美国东部时间）
中国在亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席
霍尔木兹海峡地震发生九个月后，能源安全问题被提上上周日本-东盟和亚太经济合作组织 (APEC) 峰会的议程。五年来的第二次价格冲击迫使亚洲政策制定者重新考虑能源安全规划和机构，但中国并没有带头，尽管它在地区能源安全中发挥着重要作用。
中国的优先事项是国内而非地区
作为世界上最大的石油进口国，中国与经历霍尔木兹海峡供应中断的邻国依赖进口的国家有很多共同点。然而，关于新的合作能源安全规划机制和机构的新兴区域政策讨论基本上没有提及这一点。
在过去的八个月里，中国一直专注于国内能源优先事项，其行为有时会损害其他亚洲进口商。美国和以色列袭击伊朗仅一周后，中国就禁止了几乎所有石油产品的出口许可证。中国在随后几个月放松了这些限制，但在柴油和其他燃料库存大幅下降后，十月份北京再次限制产品出口。
中国只是东亚第三大石油产品出口国（仅次于韩国和新加坡），但其出口配额的意外变化改变了市场平衡。例如，2025 年，中国供应了澳大利亚近三分之一的航空燃油进口，因此 3 月份的航空燃油禁令让澳大利亚航空公司纷纷寻找替代品。
更广泛地说，中国缺乏透明度给邻国带来了挑战。其2025年至2026年3月的库存增加支撑了全球石油需求，而炼油厂开工率下降、国内燃料价格上限和出口限制等综合因素导致2月至6月原油进口出现前所未有的下降。分析师指出，中国在石油市场的定价能力源于其原油购买的时间和数量。然而，虽然国内考虑推动了这些决定，但它们往往让中国的邻国围绕其行动进行规划。尽管宣布建立东盟-中国能源合作伙伴关系，但其邻国有理由对中国的承诺持谨慎态度。
在经历了能源危机最初几个月的急剧下降之后，亚洲石油进口已经反弹。但这次中断影响了所有依赖中东石油和天然气的进口商。日本通常 90% 以上的原油从中东进口，因此被迫从美国或拉丁美洲寻找替代品（9 月份，美国原油占日本进口量的 27%，高于去年的 3%）。通常从中东进口大部分液化石油气的印度已转向美国供应。其他亚洲进口商一直在努力获取石化原料。
进口商正在重新评估他们的供应商关系。正如国际能源署 (IEA) 执行董事法提赫·比罗尔 (Fatih Birol) 在 2026 年 4 月大西洋理事会活动中所说，进口商现在有三个重要目标：“能源来源多元化。能源结构多元化。贸易路线多元化。”对于长期依赖石油的亚洲进口商来说，这是一项艰巨的任务。

China’s conspicuous absence in Asian energy security plans - Atlantic Council
China East Asia Energy & Environment Geopolitics & Energy Security
November 25, 2026 • 10:04am ET
China’s conspicuous absence in Asian energy security plans
Nine months into the Strait of Hormuz shock, energy security was on the agenda at last week’s Japan-ASEAN and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summits. The second price shock in five years has forced Asian policymakers to rethink energy security planning and institutions—but China is not leading the charge despite its significant role in regional energy security.
China’s priorities are domestic, not regional
As the world’s largest oil importer, China has much in common with neighboring import-dependent countries weathering the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption. Yet it is largely absent from emerging regional policy discussions over new cooperative energy security planning mechanisms and institutions.
Over the past eight months, China has focused on domestic energy priorities—and its actions have sometimes harmed other Asian importers. Only a week after the US and Israeli attack on Iran, China banned export licenses for nearly all petroleum products. China relaxed those restrictions in subsequent months, but in October—after a significant decline in stocks of diesel and other fuels—Beijing again restricted product exports.
China is only the third largest petroleum product exporter in East Asia (after South Korea and Singapore), but unexpected changes to its export quotas alter market balances. For example, China supplied nearly one-third of Australia’s jet fuel imports in 2025, so its March jet fuel ban left Australian airlines scrambling for alternatives.
More broadly, China’s lack of transparency creates challenges for its neighbors. Its 2025-March 2026 inventory builds supported global oil demand, while a combination of lower refinery runs, caps on domestic fuel prices, and export restrictions contributed to an unprecedented decline in crude imports between February and June. Analysts note that China’s pricing power in oil markets stems from the timing and volume of its crude purchases. But while domestic considerations drive these decisions, they often leave China’s neighbors to plan around its actions. Despite the announcement of an ASEAN-China Energy Cooperation Partnership, its neighbors have reason to be cautious about China’s commitment.
After steep declines in the early months of the energy shock, Asian oil imports have rebounded. But the disruption has affected all importers that depend on Middle Eastern oil and gas. Japan typically imports more than 90 percent of its crude oil from the Middle East, so it has been forced to find alternatives from the United States or Latin America (in September, US crude oil accounted for 27 percent of Japan’s imports, up from 3 percent the previous year). India, which normally imports most of its liquefied petroleum gas from the Middle East, has turned to the United States for supply. Other Asian importers have struggled to secure petrochemicals feedstocks.
Importers are re-evaluating their supplier relationships. As International Energy Agency (IEA) Executive Director Fatih Birol stated at an April 2026 Atlantic Council event, importers now have three important objectives: “Diversify from whom you get your energy. Diversify your energy mix. And diversify your trade routes.” This is a difficult task for Asian importers with longstanding dependence on the Middle East, especially those with refineries configured to process crude oil grades from the Gulf and Iraq.
Addressing energy security threats with new institutions
Governments in the region see two major threats to their energy security. First, the shale revolution and the decline in US oil imports have given Washington freer rein to act in ways that can raise their energy costs and jeopardize supplies. And second, that global energy security institutions are no longer fit for purpose, since they were created amid the 1970s oil shocks—when Asia made up a much smaller share of the global economy and global oil and gas consumption.
Energy leaders see a need for new Asian energy security architecture, as governments seek to diversify supplies, build inventories, and explore joint purchasing and sharing mechanisms. Japan aims to lead this effort and has proposed several new programs to bolster energy security.
In Manila last week, leaders from Japan and Southeast Asia updated plans for the Tokyo-led Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) initiative and the related Partnership on Wide Energy and Resource Resilience Asia (POWERR Asia) framework. The AZEC action plan emphasizes cooperation on emissions reductions, carbon removal, and decarbonization of the transportation sector. Takaichi also proposed a new Asian oil security task force and referred to it as “an Asian version of the International Energy Agency.”
In April, Japan committed up to 1.5 trillion yen ($9.4 billion) under POWERR Asia to support regional procurement of new hydrocarbon supplies, infrastructure to bolster fuel storage and supply chain resilience in Asia, and diversification of energy sources. State institutions including the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC) and Japan Bank for International Cooperation are expected to support these plans that aim to broadly support Asian energy security. In several bills expected to be approved by Japan’s Diet in December, Takaichi’s government tasks JOGMEC with investing in alternative supply infrastructure including bypass pipelines and storage facilities.
At the Japan-ASEAN summit in Manila, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also proposed a new “POWERR Gulf” initiative to enhance cooperation between oil exporters in the Gulf and Asian importers. Inventories will likely be a key focus. Japan in particular is already building on existing joint stockpiling with Gulf national oil companies Saudi Aramco, Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, and Kuwait Petroleum Corporation. On November 20, Saudi Arabia and Japan announced an expanded joint oil stockpiling program. Japan intends to buy 8 million barrels of Saudi crude oil to replenish its stockpiles, and will lend Saudi Arabia new crude oil storage capacity of 16 million barrels, in addition to Aramco’s current 8.2 million barrels of capacity. Under Japan’s current joint oil stockpiling program, Gulf national oil companies lease storage capacity and use it for commercial operations in normal times, but Japanese companies have preferential rights to this crude oil in times of emergency. If the broader region embraces POWERR Gulf, the Gulf-Japan arrangement could become a template for other nations.
Asia will need more than one energy blueprint
The effectiveness of these new energy security initiatives remains to be seen. Japan and other countries in the region will remain highly dependent on the Middle East for crude oil and petroleum products. Energy resource endowments and energy systems also vary greatly across ASEAN countries, so their vulnerabilities and planning principles may differ from one country to the next.
Governments also face a strategic choice. After the second oil and gas price shock in five years, some policymakers in Southeast Asia and South Asia may lean toward more drastic changes in energy policy to emphasize resilience and use of domestic energy resources. Governments in these regions may well decide to direct scarce resources toward expanding electrification, renewable energy generation, battery storage, and grid resilience rather than new fossil fuel infrastructure.
It is notable that Japan is playing such a prominent role in region-wide energy security initiatives. This is unsurprising, since import-dependent Japan excels in long-term energy security planning and policy, including through its Strategic Energy Plans. Some officials and analysts in the broader region, however, worry that the proposed frameworks are too focused on fossil fuels, arguing that new investment should focus on electrification and renewable energy.
Opportunities for energy security leadership
As Asian governments devise new plans and institutions to bolster energy security and resilience, China is both absent and inescapable. China is the world’s largest oil importer, holds the world’s largest oil stockpiles, and is a key customer for nearly all the Gulf countries. More than any other importer, its actions will affect prices and energy security for its neighbors.
Beyond the oil and gas sector, China’s “electrostate” model and its many innovations in electrification, electric vehicle manufacturing, battery technology, and clean energy deployment will be important for Asian countries seeking to cut import dependence and build energy resilience. Yet it is not playing an especially active role in emerging multilateral discussions about how to bolster energy security in Asia. China’s lack of transparency and focus on domestic issues leaves a policy and planning gap that Japan is well positioned to fill.

title: Tentara Nasional Indonesia Angkatan Laut, U.S. Navy commence CARAT Indonesia 2026
zh_title: 印度尼西亚国家陆军海军和美国海军启动 CARAT Indonesia 2026
summary: 2026 年 11 月 25 日，印度尼西亚泗水（2026 年 11 月 25 日）——来自美国第七舰队和印度尼西亚国家海军部队 (TNI-AL) 的海防部队于 11 月 25 日在泗水举行会议，开始印度尼西亚海上合作准备和训练 (CARAT)。第 32 届 CARAT 印度尼西亚演习以开幕式启动，以美国和印度尼西亚之间之前的海上演习和行动为基础。 CARAT是一项海上演习，旨在促进地区安全合作，维护和加强海上伙伴关系，增强参演部队之间的互操作性
content:
2026 年 11 月 25 日

印度尼西亚泗水（2026 年 11 月 25 日）——来自美国第七舰队和印度尼西亚国家海军部队 (TNI-AL) 的海防部队于 11 月 25 日在泗水召开会议，开始印度尼西亚海上合作准备和训练 (CARAT)。

第 32 届 CARAT 印度尼西亚演习以开幕式启动，以美国和印度尼西亚之间之前的海上演习和行动为基础。 CARAT是一项海上演习，旨在促进地区安全合作，维护和加强海上伙伴关系，增强参演部队之间的互操作性。

美国驻泗水总领事克里斯·格林表示：“CARAT 代表了美国和印度尼西亚共同致力于促进整个印度-太平洋地区的海上安全和战备。” “30 多年来，CARAT 不断增强我们在广泛的海军能力领域并肩工作的能力。”
第 77 特遣部队 (CTF) 指挥官的复仇者级反水雷舰 USS Warrior (MCM 10) 于 11 月 25 日抵达印度尼西亚，启动初步活动。演习的海上阶段还将有来自 CTF-72 的一架 P-8A 海神海上巡逻和侦察机、三艘 TNI-AL 西格玛级护卫舰、法尼级反水雷舰 KRI Pulau Fani (MCMV 731) 和 KRI Pulau Fanildo (MCMV 732)、两架空客 AS656 Panther 直升机和一架 TNI-AL CN 235 飞机。 TNI-AL。此次迭代的海上阶段将以反潜战演习、水雷对抗最佳实践以及水面行动小组协调来进行跨部队指挥和控制为特色。

支持 CARAT 印度尼西亚 2026 的其他人员和工作人员包括美国第七舰队中队第 7 驱逐舰中队 (DESRON) 的指挥官，以及来自 CTF-73、CTF-75 和太平洋海军信息战中心的主题专家。主题专家交流 (SMEE) 主题将包括航空、网络、打捞潜水、爆炸物处理和 **U.S.-TNI-AL** 联合音乐表演。在泗水岸上举行的 SMEE 将通过建立人与人之间的关系来促进信息共享并促进海上互操作性。
“我们感谢印度尼西亚合作伙伴在泗水的热情欢迎和热情款待，”CTF-76 参谋长兼代表团团长美国海军上尉阿方扎·怀特 (Alfonza White) 说。 “CARAT 加强了我们的协调，建立了互信，并帮助我们维护了一个自由开放的印太地区。”

CARAT是一项长期演习系列，旨在增强美国及其伙伴部队共同行动应对该地区共同海上挑战的能力。

作为美国海军在东南亚前沿部署的DESRON，DESRON-7担任东南亚作战地区指定舰艇的主要战术和作战指挥官。

美国第七舰队是海军最大的前沿部署编号舰队，经常与盟友和伙伴互动和行动，以维护自由开放的印度太平洋地区。

25 November 2026

SURABAYA, Indonesia (Nov. 25, 2026) — Maritime defense forces from U.S. 7th Fleet and Tentara Nasional Indonesia Angkatan Laut (TNI-AL) convened in Surabaya, Nov. 25, to commence Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) Indonesia.

The 32nd iteration of CARAT Indonesia launched with an opening ceremony, building upon previous maritime exercises and operations between the U.S. and Indonesia. CARAT is a maritime exercise designed to promote regional security cooperation, maintain and strengthen maritime partnerships, and enhance interoperability among participating forces.

“CARAT represents a commitment shared by the United States and Indonesia to promote maritime security and readiness across the Indo-Pacific,” said Chris Green, U.S. Consul General in Surabaya. “After more than 30 years, CARAT continues to enhance our ability to work side-by-side across a wide range of naval competencies.”

Avenger-class mine countermeasures ship USS Warrior (MCM 10) from Commander, Task Force (CTF) 77 arrived in Indonesia, Nov. 25, to kick off preliminary events. The sea-phase of the exercise will also feature a P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft from CTF-72, as well as three TNI-AL Sigma-class corvettes, Fani-class mine countermeasures vessels KRI Pulau Fani (MCMV 731) and KRI Pulau Fanildo (MCMV 732), two Airbus AS656 Panther helicopters, and one TNI-AL CN 235 aircraft from TNI-AL. The sea-phase of this iteration will feature anti-submarine warfare drills, mine countermeasures best practices, and surface action group coordination to exercise command and control across units.

Additional personnel and staff supporting CARAT Indonesia 2026 include Commander, Destroyer Squadron (DESRON) 7, the U.S. 7th Fleet Band, and subject matter experts from CTF-73, CTF-75, and Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific. Subject matter expert exchange (SMEE) topics will include aviation, cyber, salvage diving, explosive ordnance disposal, and **U.S.–TNI-AL** combined musical performances. The SMEEs, held ashore in Surabaya, will facilitate information-sharing and promote interoperability at sea through building people-to-people relationships.

“We are grateful to our Indonesian partners for their warm welcome and hospitality in Surabaya,” said U.S. Navy Capt. Alfonza White, chief of staff, CTF-76, and head of delegation. “CARAT strengthens our coordination, builds mutual trust, and helps us preserve a free and open Indo-Pacific.”

CARAT is a long-standing exercise series designed to enhance U.S. and partner forces abilities to operate together in response to shared maritime challenges in the region.

As the U.S. Navy’s forward-deployed DESRON in Southeast Asia, DESRON-7 serves as the primary tactical and operational commander of assigned ships in the Southeast Asia area of operations.

U.S. 7th Fleet, the Navy’s largest forward-deployed numbered fleet, routinely interacts and operates with allies and partners in preserving a free and open Indo-Pacific.

content:
香港船东欢呼航运税改革 - Splash247
香港船东协会（HKSOA）欢迎一系列旨在吸引更多航运和大宗商品贸易企业来到香港的税收改革，其中包括针对实物大宗商品贸易商的新的半税率利得税优惠。
该措施于周三返回立法会审议，将把合资格商品贸易活动的利得税税率从16.5%下调至8.25%，同时扩大对船舶租赁、船舶管理、船舶代理和经纪业务的现有优惠。
该立法还为经合组织全球最低税率规则涵盖的合格航运公司和大宗商品贸易商引入了可选的 15% 税率，使他们能够简化 BEPS 2.0 框架下的合规工作。
对于船舶出租人来说，这些变化包括更广泛地扣除船舶购置成本和融资费用，以及租赁安排的更大灵活性。
商品贸易特许权旨在吸引更多贸易公司来到香港，并产生对本地航运服务的额外需求。
根据拟议的框架，符合资格的贸易商必须满足最低营业额和本地运营要求，包括将海事服务支出与香港供应商联系起来的条件。
政府此前估计，这些特许权可以通过鼓励大宗商品贸易商在香港建立或扩大业务来产生 46 亿港元（5.9 亿美元）的经济效益。
HKSOA主席Richard Hext表示，这些措施体现了政府、立法者和航运业之间的合作。
“航运业是一个竞争激烈的行业，需要许多社区利益相关者的支持，包括政府和立法者，”赫克斯说。
“新的税收措施是公私合作的一个很好的例子。每一项此类举措都增加了香港作为全球海事之都的吸引力。”
该协会代表 200 多家航运和海事相关企业，表示将与税务局合作，帮助该行业适应新要求。
自2020年以来，香港一直向合格的船舶出租商提供优惠税收待遇，并在随后的几年中向船舶租赁管理公司和其他商业海事服务提供商提供优惠。最新的改革是政府为加强该市作为海事金融、航运和大宗商品贸易中心的作用而做出的更广泛努力的一部分。

The Hong Kong Shipowners Association (HKSOA) has welcomed a package of tax reforms aimed at attracting more shipping and commodity trading businesses to the city, including a new half-rate profits tax concession for physical commodity traders.
The measures, which returned to the Legislative Council for consideration on Wednesday, would reduce the profits tax rate on qualifying commodity trading activities from 16.5% to 8.25%, while expanding existing concessions for ship leasing, shipmanagement, ship agency and broking businesses.
The legislation also introduces an optional 15% tax rate for qualifying shipping companies and commodity traders covered by the OECD’s global minimum tax rules, allowing them to simplify compliance under the BEPS 2.0 framework.
For ship lessors, the changes include broader deductions for vessel acquisition costs and financing expenses, alongside greater flexibility in leasing arrangements.
The commodity trading concession is designed to bring more trading houses to Hong Kong and generate additional demand for local shipping services.
Under the proposed framework, eligible traders must meet minimum business turnover and local operating requirements, including conditions linking expenditure on maritime services to Hong Kong-based providers.
The government has previously estimated that the concessions could generate HK$4.6bn ($590m) in economic benefits by encouraging commodity traders to establish or expand their operations in the city.
HKSOA chairman Richard Hext said the measures reflected cooperation between the government, legislators and the shipping industry.
“The shipping sector is a highly competitive industry, requiring the support of many community stakeholders, including the government and legislators,” Hext said.
“The new tax measures are an excellent example of public-private partnership. Each and every such initiative adds to Hong Kong’s attraction as a global maritime capital.”
The association, which represents more than 200 shipping and maritime-related businesses, said it would work with the Inland Revenue Department to help the industry adapt to the new requirements.
Hong Kong has been offering preferential tax treatment to qualifying ship lessors since 2020, extending concessions to ship leasing managers and other commercial maritime service providers in subsequent years. The latest reforms form part of the government’s wider effort to strengthen the city’s role as a maritime finance, shipping and commodity trading centre.

title: Survivors battle pain, loss one year after deadly Hong Kong blaze
zh_title: 香港致命火灾一年后，幸存者与痛苦和损失作斗争
summary: 叶家驹在香港数十年来最严重的火灾中幸存下来，但他失去了家园和妻子。他们半融化的结婚戒指是他们生命中仅存的少数痕迹之一。 2025年12月2日，香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑致命火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。 2025 年 11 月 26 日，香港一处住宅区发生毁灭性火灾，造成 168 人死亡，一年后，幸存者和失去亲人的家庭正在为失去亲人而苦苦挣扎。法新社采访了 1980 年以来世界上最致命的住宅楼火灾的幸存者：68 岁的叶家驹 (Yip Ka-kui Yip) 经常发现
content:
叶家驹在香港数十年来最严重的火灾中幸存下来，但他失去了家园和妻子。他们半融化的结婚戒指是他们生命中仅存的少数痕迹之一。 2025年12月2日，香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑致命火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。 2025 年 11 月 26 日，香港一处住宅区发生毁灭性火灾，造成 168 人死亡，一年后，幸存者和失去亲人的家庭正在为失去亲人而苦苦挣扎。法新社采访了 1980 年以来世界上最致命的住宅楼火灾的幸存者：68 岁的叶家驹 (Yip Ka-kui Yip) 经常沿着他与结婚四十年的妻子白水莲 (Pak Shui-lin) 一起走过的公寓大楼的路线走下去，他说自己仍然“无法接受”她的去世。幸存者表示，朴通过敲邻居的门提醒他们发生火灾而挽救了生命。日常生活中的简单时刻让叶想起她的缺席。他说，就好像“她在家里等我回来”。他仍然向妻子的号码发送生活动态，例如孙女的成绩单。叶先生还送来了半融化的结婚戒指进行修复，希望从废墟中打捞出来的物品可以代代相传，以纪念这一事件。他告诉法新社，政府的道歉“缺乏诚意”，并补充说他希望社会确保“正义得到伸张”。
38 岁的楚楚 (Chu Chu) 回忆起一名验尸官掀起覆盖着他 76 岁父亲烧焦遗体的布，他的遗体是从被掏空的公寓里找到的，骨灰在空气中翻滚。 来自 Getty Images 的嵌入 “感觉就像我的父亲真的消失在时间的沙子里一样，”他说。 “我觉得我还没有找到我的父亲。火灾发生前不久，我还能和他说话。我仍然无法理解我在太平间看到的实际上是他。”他 45 岁的姐姐也担心，在父亲的物品被毁后，她们对父亲的记忆可能会“消失”。她仍然保留着他在火灾发生前六天送给她儿子的生日牛奶糖。他们的父亲曾是殖民时代英国驻军的车辆修理工和夜班出租车司机。兄弟姐妹说，他在火灾中幸存下来的物品包括一把军刀和一罐 50 美分的硬币——象征着他的勤奋精神和对家庭无条件的爱。 61岁的何贝蒂(Betty Ho Ho)在该住宅区居住了35年，并用了20年的时间还清了公寓的贷款。当她说火灾“夺走了我的一切”时，她刚刚开始享受退休生活。对何来说，这场悲剧揭示了“整个体系和政府结构的问题”。她说，官员们在火灾发生前没有听取居民的投诉。她现在住在政府安排的临时住房里，但不愿意把它称为家。
与大多数其他居民不同，何女士没有接受政府买断，而是要求在同一地点重建住宅区，这一提议被当局拒绝。“那所房子离得很近，但你不能回去，”她在现在的住所说，从那里她可以看到她的旧公寓。何说，灾难发生一年后，她感到“无助”。 “未来五年是不可能的，我什至无法想象。” Harry Leung Leung 是最后一批逃离火灾的居民之一。 “我们没有好好地告别我们住了这么久的地方，”20多岁、从小就住在公寓里的梁说。他说他走了

【原文 English Original】
Yip Ka-kui survived Hong Kong’s deadliest fire in decades, but he lost his home and his wife. Their half-melted wedding rings are among the few traces that remain of their lives. Hongkongers pay tribute on December 2, 2025, to the victims who died in the fatal fire in Tai Po Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. A year after the devastating November 26, 2025 fire killed 168 people in a Hong Kong housing estate, survivors and bereaved families are struggling with their loss. AFP spoke to survivors of the world’s deadliest residential building blaze since 1980: Yip Ka-kui Yip, 68, often finds himself retracing the path to the apartment complex that he used to take with his wife of four decades, Pak Shui-lin, whose death he says he still “cannot accept”. Embed from Getty Images Survivors say Pak saved lives by knocking on neighbours’ doors to alert them to the fire. Simple moments of daily life remind Yip of her absence. It’s as though “she is at home waiting for me to return”, he said. He still sends life updates, such as their granddaughter’s report card, to his wife’s number. Yip also sent their half-melted wedding rings for restoration, hoping that objects salvaged from the ruins can be passed down through generations as a reminder of the incident. The government’s apology “lacked sincerity”, he told AFP, adding that he hoped the society would ensure “justice is served”. Chu Chu, 38, recalled a coroner lifting the cloth covering his 76-year-old father’s charred remains recovered from their gutted flat, stirring ashes into the air. Embed from Getty Images “It felt like my dad was actually vanishing into the sands of time,” he said. “I feel like I haven’t found my dad. Not long before the fire, I could still talk to him. “I still can’t fathom what I saw in the mortuary was actually him.” His 45-year-old sister also fears their memories of their father might “drift away” after his belongings were destroyed. She still keeps the milk candies he gave her son for his birthday, six days before the fire. Their father used to work as a vehicle mechanic for the colonial-era British garrison and as a night-shift taxi driver. Among his belongings that survived the fire were a military blade and a jar of 50-cent coins — symbols of his hardworking spirit and unconditional love for the family, the siblings said. Betty Ho Ho, 61, lived in the housing estate for 35 years and spent two decades paying off her apartment. Embed from Getty Images She had just begun to enjoy retirement when she said the fire “took everything away from me”. For Ho, the tragedy revealed “problems with the entire system and the government structure”. Officials, she said, failed to heed residents’ complaints before the fire. She now lives in government-arranged temporary housing, but is reluctant to call it home. Unlike most other residents, Ho did not accept a government buyout and instead called for the housing complex to be rebuilt on the same site — a proposal rejected by authorities. “That home is so close, but you can’t go back,” she said at her current residence, from which she can see her old flat. Ho said she felt “helpless” a year after the disaster. “It’s impossible to think about the next five years, I can’t even imagine it.” Harry Leung Leung was among the last residents to escape the fire. “We didn’t properly say goodbye to a place where we had lived for so long,” said Leung, who was in his late 20s and had lived in the flat since childhood. He said he took the government’s buyout offer out of necessity. Wang Fuk Court on November 26, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “(The officials) had sugarcoated this as a mutually agreeable transaction,” he told AFP. As part of the buyout scheme, he bought another property but was saddled with more than HK$1 million (US$128,000) in debt. That financial burden was “never part of my life plan”, he added. “I’m still young… but for other residents who have already retired and may have little income, such change is an overburden for them.” Rhodora Alcaraz Tunacao Tunacao, 29, was a Filipino migrant domestic worker widely hailed as a hero for protecting a three-month-old baby girl during the fire one day after starting work in Hong Kong. Embed from Getty Images After being treated in the intensive care unit for smoke inhalation, she returned to the Philippines in December. But she remains under emotional stress, according to Esther Tse, an advocate for workers rights who visits her regularly. Tunacao also suffers from lung problems, requiring regular follow-ups and medication, Tse said. At times, she coughed up black phlegm. She needs depression medication and is easily agitated, but mental health professionals are scarce in her region, Tse added.

title: Wang Fuk Court fire tragedy: Why Hong Kong’s works regulation must break from civil service culture
zh_title: 宏福苑火灾惨案：为何香港的工程规管必须脱离公务员文化
summary: 宏福阁大火夺去了168人的生命，一年后，让我们考虑一下政府的应对措施是否足够。当局道歉，住房局局长何温妮辞职。这些都是值得欢迎的举措，现在的重点是改革。但有一个问题很突出：香港的监管质量明显参差不齐。香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。世界银行对香港的监管制度给予高度评价。该城市在全球约 200 个地区中排名第八，在亚洲排名第二，仅次于新加坡（全球排名第二）
content:
宏福阁大火夺去了168人的生命，一年后，让我们考虑一下政府的应对措施是否足够。当局道歉，住房局局长何温妮辞职。这些都是值得欢迎的举措，现在的重点是改革。但有一个问题很突出：香港的监管质量明显参差不齐。香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。世界银行对香港的监管制度给予高度评价。该城市在全球约 200 个地区中排名第八，在亚洲排名第二，仅次于新加坡（全球排名第一）。然而，我们在宏福苑火灾悲剧和其他与工程相关的丑闻中却表现出了监管的无能。调查火灾的独立审查委员会将监管失误描述为“系统性和普遍性”。香港在金融服务、公共卫生、诚信（反腐败）和其他领域的监管无疑相对较好。因此评价很高。因此，我们不能说工程监管的缺位和/或不力（不仅是宏福苑火灾，还有玛丽医院电梯事件、太宗电梯防火板事件等）代表了整个香港的公共监管。问题是，为什么建筑监管如此草率和参差不齐，明显优先考虑行政便利，或许还保护建筑业？
政府的工务部门历史悠久，是殖民地香港最早的政府职能之一，人员全部由公务员组成。当局于 1843 年设立测量总署。1870 年演变为测量部，并于 1883 年更名为工务署 (PWD)。工务署管理所有工务职能。 1982 年，官员们将这个庞然大物拆分为七个工程部门。它们大多由现任发展局局长监管。该报告向我们表明，几十年来，监管制度未能充分优先考虑服务和保护公众的情况一直被容忍。那些领导建筑和建设的人大多是从公务员队伍内部提拔的，公务员队伍分为专业队伍。新入职的公务员在进入时就已经融入了本部门实践中的价值观。团队领导者和团队成员执行非正式规范，指导新进入者应如何行事以及对他们的期望。接受这些非正式规范对于在部门中相处和取得进步是必要的。 “不要破坏现状”的文化占主导地位。官僚问责制度在这些规范内运作。官僚文化具有“粘性”，难以改变。现在想想我们表现良好的监管机构：香港金融管理局、证券及期货事务监察委员会、廉政公署。
在最近的各个时期，这些当局都是在公务员系统之外设立的。在这些当局中，当局优先考虑的是与过去的做法的彻底决裂。独立委员会关于宏福苑火灾的报告副本，2026 年 10 月 29 日。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。委员会对火灾的审查报告特别指出了住房部门独立检查组（ICU）的行为。独立审查组本应监督宏福苑的外墙翻新和维护工作，批准计划、进行检查并确保符合建筑安全标准。作者

【原文 English Original】
A year on from the Wang Fuk Court blaze, which claimed 168 lives, let’s consider whether the government’s response is sufficient. Authorities apologised and housing chief Winnie Ho resigned. These are welcome moves, and the focus now is on reform. But one area stands out: Hong Kong’s apparently uneven regulatory quality. Hongkongers pay tribute to victims who died in the fatal fire in Tai Po Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. The World Bank rates Hong Kong’s regulatory regime highly. The city ranks eighth out of some 200 territories globally and second in Asia after Singapore (globally ranked as No. 1). And yet we have demonstrated regulatory incapacity in the Wang Fuk Court fire tragedy and other works-related scandals. The independent review committee looking into the blaze described the regulatory failings as “ systematic and pervasive .” Hong Kong regulates financial services, public health, integrity (anti-corruption) and undoubtedly other areas relatively well. Hence the high rating. So, we cannot say that absent and/or poor works regulation (not only the Wang Fuk Court fire disaster, but the Queen Mary Hospital elevator case , the Taizoom elevator fire panel case , etc.) is representative of Hong Kong public regulation as a whole. The question is why building and construction regulation is so sloppy and uneven, apparently prioritising administrative convenience and perhaps protecting the construction industry? The works side of the government is ancient, created among the earliest government functions in colonial Hong Kong and staffed entirely by civil servants. Authorities set up the Surveyor General’s Office in 1843. It morphed into the Survey Department in 1870, and was renamed the Public Works Department (PWD) in 1883. PWD managed all works functions. In 1982, officials broke up this behemoth into seven works departments. They are mostly supervised by the Secretary for Development who is still in her post. The report shows us that a regulatory regime hat failed to sufficiently prioritise serving and protecting the public was tolerated for decades. Those leading building and construction are mostly promoted from within the civil service, which is organised into professional streams. Newly hired civil servants are socialised into the values in practice of their department when they enter. Team leaders and team members enforce informal norms that guide new entrants into how they should behave and what is expected of them. Accepting these informal norms is necessary to get along and ahead in the department. A “don’t rock the boat” culture dominates. Bureaucratic accountability systems operate within these norms. Bureaucratic culture is “sticky” and difficult to change. Now consider our well-performing regulators: the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the Securities and Futures Commission, the Independent Commission Against Corruption. Each of relatively recent vintage, these authorities were set up outside the civil service. In them, authorities prioritised a sharp break from past practice. Copies of the independent committee’s report on the Wang Fuk Court fire, on October 29, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The committee review report into the fire singles out the behaviour of the housing department’s Independent Checking Unit (ICU). The ICU was supposed to supervise external wall renovation and maintenance work at Wang Fuk Court, approving plans, conducting inspections and ensuring compliance with building safety standards. Authorities classified Wang Fuk Court’s renovation as lower-risk “minor works” although it was an eye-popping HK$330 million project. This reduced the statutory level of ICU oversight required. The unit was also responsible for investigating and addressing residents’ reports and safety complaints. The report noted in particular the ICU’s “lack of sense of crisis, regulatory lapses, systemic blind spots, and enforcement failures.” This is a damning judgement. The ICU is composed of senior professionals including many structural engineers, maintenance surveyors, architects, and technical staff. Not only did the ICU fail in its duty to serve and protect citizens, but the professionals among them failed in their duty to uphold the values of professionalism, integrity, and excellence. The government set up a new public housing building control section which is welcome. But transferring the existing ICU staff who bring with them values in practice that led to the tragedy is a mistake. I urge the government to set up a new body outside the existing works bureaucracy. Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on December 2, 2025, days after a fatal fire engulfed seven of the eight blocks of the residential estate. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. Beyond government, action is needed too. Professional bodies should enforce discipline among their members. Many professionals were involved in the various works scandals. Professional bodies such as the Engineers Registration Board should investigate those involved, and if found culpable, take action with consequences, such as suspending or cancelling their licences to practise in Hong Kong. title: HKFP Lens: A year of grief and inquiry, after Tai Po blaze
zh_title: HKFP 镜头：大埔大火后悲痛与质询的一年
summary: 宏福苑是一个建于 20 世纪 80 年代靠近吐露港的八座住宅屋村，拥有近 2,000 户家庭。消防处于 2026 年 11 月 26 日对宏福苑致命火灾作出反应。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。大埔综合楼的家庭辛辛苦苦买了一套舒适的公寓并养育了他们的孩子——其中一些人后来成为了公寓的业主，在同一片土地上养育了第三代。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，大埔致命火灾发生一天后，一名男子站在被毁坏的宏福苑屋苑前。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
content:
宏福苑是一个建于 20 世纪 80 年代靠近吐露港的八座住宅屋村，拥有近 2,000 户家庭。消防处于 2026 年 11 月 26 日对宏福苑致命火灾作出反应。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。大埔综合楼的家庭辛辛苦苦买了一套舒适的公寓并养育了他们的孩子——其中一些人后来成为了公寓的业主，在同一片土地上养育了第三代。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，大埔致命火灾发生一天后，一名男子站在被毁坏的宏福苑屋苑前。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。它曾是香港梦的缩影，直到去年11月26日下午，社区发生致命火灾。由于当时正在进行大规模翻修工程，火势迅速蔓延到八栋用泡沫板和脚手架网覆盖的建筑物中的七栋。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，家人在辨认大埔大火受害者亲人的尸体后哭泣。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。在平常的工作日下午，老年人、儿童、全职妈妈、夜班后休息的爸爸以及家政工人都被困在火灾中。 2025年11月28日，在致命的大埔火灾中失去家园的人们暂时住在广福村的大厅，这是一个公共屋村，靠近遭受火灾的宏福苑。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
这场大火最终夺去了 168 人的生命，导致数千人无家可归，标志着充满无尽悲伤、愤怒和疑问的一年的开始。香港摄影记者回顾了过去一年的照片，我们的摄影记者跟踪了香港数十年来最严重火灾后的重大事件和事态发展。火灾发生后，数以千计的香港人动员线上线下支持受害者。照片显示，2025 年 11 月 27 日，志愿者在宏福法院附近集会，设立摊位，提供免费食物、衣服和生活用品。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025 年 12 月 1 日，人们在大埔地铁里阅读对火灾受害者的支持信息。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025年12月5日，数千人献花和玩偶，哀悼宏福苑火灾中的遇难者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025 年 12 月 1 日，一名学生在哀悼死者时流下了眼泪。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025 年 12 月 1 日，道士为死者举行仪式。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。火灾发生后，宏福苑部分建筑物发现非阻燃脚手架网。后来被证实是导致火势迅速蔓延的原因之一。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。火灾发生后不久，立法会于 2025 年 12 月 7 日举行选举。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 11月底，香港警务处命令义工拆除广福村平台的临时补给站。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
2025 年 12 月 19 日，消防员聚集在一起哀悼在大埔火灾中因公殉职的消防员何伟豪。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。悲剧发生后，2026年1月16日，宏福苑居民江志强（左一）、李家强（中）和叶家驹（右一）回忆起居民如何徒劳地试图报告火灾风险。他们敦促政府调查火灾原因。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2026年2月5日，独立委员会召开了上市前第一次公开会议。

【原文 English Original】
Wang Fuk Court, an eight-block residential estate built in the 1980s near Tolo Harbour, was home to nearly 2,000 households. The Fire Services Department responds to the fatal blaze at Wang Fuk Court on November 26, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The families at the Tai Po complex had worked hard to purchase a comfortable flat and raise their children – some of whom later became flat owners, bringing up a third generation on the same estate. On November 27, 2025, one day after the fatal Tai Po fire started, a man stands in front of the ravaged Wang Fuk Court housing estate. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The blaze quickly spread through seven of the eight buildings which were covered with foam board and scaffolding nets, as a large-scale renovation project was underway at the time. Seniors, children, full-time moms, dads who were taking a break after night shifts, and domestic workers were among those trapped in the fire during the otherwise ordinary weekday afternoon. HKFP looks back at images from the past year, as our photojournalist followed the major events and developments surrounding the aftermath of Hong Kong’s worst fire in decades. Following the fire, thousands of Hongkongers mobilised online and offline to support victims. People read supportive messages for the fire victims in a subway in Tai Po on December 1, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A student sheds tears while mourning the deceased on December 1, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Taoist priests hold rituals for the deceased on December 1, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Following the fire, non-flame retardant scaffolding nets were identified on some buildings of Wang Fuk Court. They were later confirmed as one of the causes leading to the rapid spread of the blaze. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Soon after the fire, the Legislative Council held elections on December 7, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In late November, the Hong Kong Police Force orders volunteers to remove the makeshift supply stations at a podium of Kwong Fuk Estate. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On December 19, 2025, firefighters gathered and mourned Ho Wai Ho, a firefighter who died in the line of duty during the Tai Po fire. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Following the tragedy, on January 16, 2026, Wang Fuk Court residents Jason Kong (first from left), Garrick Lee (middle) and Yip Ka-kui (first from right) recalled how residents made futile attempts to flag fire risks. They urged the government to investigate the causes of the fire. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On February 5, 2026, an independent committee held the first public meeting before starting hearings to probe the Tai Po fire. Judge David Lok (3rd left), chair of the committee, is seen walking out of the hearing. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Tony Tsui (centre right), the former chair of Wang Fuk Court owners’ corporation management committee, leaves after attending a public hearing to probe the Tai Po deadly fire on March 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A Wang Fuk Court resident talks with the press after attending a public hearing on March 26, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On April 20, 2026, nearly half a year after the fire, Wang Fuk Court residents are allowed to return to their fire-ravaged homes to retrieve belongings. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wang Fuk Court residents return home to retrieve belongings on May 4, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A resident of Wang Fuk Court is seen in his fire-ravaged flat as he looks to retrieve personal belongings on April 23, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A Wang Fuk Court resident finds his wedding rings in his flat at Wang Fuk Court on April 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The photo shows Kong leaving the Shatin Law Courts Buildings on September 1, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. content: 澳大利亚租客正迎来一些令人欣慰的生活成本缓解，一项鲜为人知的太阳能计划正帮助一些家庭大幅削减电费。 昆士兰州政府正在帮助租客降低电费，向房东提供最高3,500澳元的补贴，用于在出租房产安装太阳能板。 自去年12月启动以来，已有超过600名房东获得补贴，为租客安装太阳能系统。 据Crisafulli政府称，昆士兰州民的电价正在下降，该州东南部居民的电价降幅在7.2%至10.7%之间，而偏远城镇居民的电价降幅为7%。 不到12个月内，该计划已收到超过1,000份申请，其中600份已完成，400份待评估，大多数已安装系统超过5千瓦，从而获得全额3,500澳元补贴。 财政部长兼能源部长David Janetzki表示，“Supercharged Solar for Renters”计划旨在为辛勤工作的昆士兰州民提供具有成本效益的生活方式。 “房东们已经加入进来，租客们正从更便宜的电费账单中获益。这种缓解对家庭产生了真正的改变，”Janetzki说。 租客享受更便宜太阳能的回报 昆士兰州政府转述了房东和租客关于“Supercharged Solar for Renters”计划如何为他们双方省钱的故事。 房东Dave Pritchard表示，补贴使安装太阳能更加负担得起。另一方面，租客Stacey Kerr表示，拥有太阳能开辟了新的节省渠道。 “自从安装太阳能系统以来，与去年相比，我们的电费账单减少了一半，”Kerr说。 “对于租客来说，这是显著的节省，对我们日常家庭开支产生了真正的改变。” 昆士兰州在Energex和Ergon Energy网络中共有超过90万套屋顶太阳能系统接入，参与计划的房东必须使用Crisafulli政府能源路线图下持牌、认证的安装商。

content: 随着厄尔尼诺现象（El Niño）持续增强，澳大利亚气象局（Bureau of Meteorology）预测，今年夏季澳大利亚几乎整个大陆都可能出现高于平均水平的气温，民众或将迎来一个格外炎热的夏天。 除了西澳大利亚州埃克斯茅斯（Exmouth）附近一小段沿海地区外，澳大利亚全国各地出现异常高温的可能性都在增加。 气象局气候学家 Qian Zhou 表示，澳大利亚北部、西部以及东部远端地区，出现异常高温的风险尤其高。 气象局确认，今年10月是有记录以来最热的10月，气温较1961年至1990年的平均水平高出 1.05摄氏度，创下自1900年以来单月最高正温度异常纪录。 根据气象局发布的夏季天气展望，这波高温天气预计将持续。其中，澳大利亚北部、塔斯马尼亚州东部，以及新州沿海的麦夸里港（Port Macquarie）一带，可能出现最极端的高温。 除了白天气温偏高，澳大利亚多个地区也可能迎来更加炎热的夜晚。 气象局预测，除西澳大利亚州加斯科因海岸（Gascoyne Coast）、南澳大利亚州南部、维多利亚州西部、新州西南部，以及塔斯马尼亚州西部外，全国大部分地区的夜间最低气温也可能高于正常水平。 与此同时，部分地区的降雨量预计偏低，尤其是塔斯马尼亚州，以及西澳大利亚州金伯利（Kimberley）和皮尔巴拉（Pilbara）沿海地区，夏季可能出现低于平均水平的降雨。 Qian Zhou 表示，厄尔尼诺现象持续增强，是导致干燥天气的重要原因之一，而全球变暖也进一步加剧了这一趋势。 虽然澳大利亚大部分地区预计天气炎热、干燥，但并非所有地区都会如此。 气象局预测，昆士兰州南部及新南威尔士州东北部部分地区，尤其是在12月，可能出现极端降雨天气。 至于澳大利亚其他地区，目前天气预测仍存在较大不确定性，暂时无法明确判断降雨量会高于还是低于正常水平。 Qian Zhou 提醒，部分地区还可能出现突发性洪水，尤其是那些流域已经处于饱和状态的地区。 这意味着，即使降雨时间不长，也可能因为地面和河流水系无法继续吸收大量雨水，而引发局部洪水。 澳大利亚发布夏季天气展望之际，北部沿海海域的海水温度也在近期明显上升。 截至11月15日当周，卡奔塔利亚湾（Gulf of Carpentaria）及珊瑚海（Coral Sea）的海面温度，比平均水平高出最多2摄氏度。 澳大利亚南部及东南部周边海域的水温则更加异常，部分地区比平均水平高出最多3摄氏度。 相比之下，澳大利亚西部海域的水温则接近或低于平均水平。 国际气候模型预测，2026年全球气温可能比工业化前水平高出1.5摄氏度以上。 与此同时，欧洲气候机构哥白尼气候变化服务局（Copernicus）公布的每日地表温度数据也显示，全球已有多个日子录得超过工业化前水平2摄氏度的升温。 全球气候持续升温，极端高温天气带来的影响正日益受到关注。 澳大利亚皇家全科医生学院（Royal Australian College of GPs）主席 Ramya Raman 表示，极端高温绝不只是普通的天气变化，而是一项不容忽视的公共卫生问题。 她指出，高温可能引发严重的健康问题，包括与热相关的疾病，甚至导致原本可以避免的死亡。 事实上，在澳大利亚，每年因极端高温造成的死亡人数及住院人数，比其他任何自然灾害都要多。 澳大利亚联邦政府在2025年发布的《气候风险评估报告》（Climate Risk Assessment）也指出，随着气候变化持续恶化，与高温相关的健康风险预计将进一步上升。 Ramya Raman 医生解释，当人体自身的散热机制无法应付外界高温时，即使是年轻、健康、平时身体状况良好的人，也可能因此生病。 她分享了一名患者的经历。这名患者平时身体健康、体能良好，去年却因为在热浪期间进行马拉松训练，最终需要入院治疗。 医生表示，尽管患者的训练计划与平时完全相同，但明显低估了高温对身体造成的影响。 最终，患者出现肌肉相关并发症，进一步影响肾脏功能。 这也说明，即使平时有运动习惯、身体素质良好，在极端高温下进行户外运动仍可能面临严重健康风险。 极端高温造成的健康影响，在全球各地已经逐渐显现。 伦敦帝国理工学院（Imperial College London）的公共卫生专家估计，今年欧洲夏季约有50,391人死于高温相关原因，而今年欧洲夏季也是有记录以来最热的夏季。 研究估计，近三分之一的高温相关死亡发生在6月最后几周至7月1日期间。当时，欧洲每日平均气温比1991年至2020年的平均水平高出超过5摄氏度。 研究人员指出，约三分之二的高温相关死亡可归因于气候变化。 这一发现也与《柳叶刀》（The Lancet）最新全球健康研究的结果一致。 该研究发现，2016年至2023年期间，全球每年有超过50万人死于与高温有关的原因，其中68%的死亡与气候变化有关。 Ramya Raman 医生表示，可以肯定的是，即将到来的澳大利亚夏季也将面临高温带来的健康挑战。 她提醒，高温可能对人体健康造成重大影响，严重时甚至会导致住院，部分情况下更可能危及生命。 夏季防暑提醒： 今年澳大利亚夏季预计将面临高温、干燥与局部极端降雨并存的天气。民众应特别留意天气预报，避免在高温时段进行剧烈户外活动，并注意补充水分。尤其是长者、儿童及有慢性疾病的人士，更应做好防暑措施，切勿低估极端高温对身体的影响。

Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

东盟和亚太经合组织：特朗普真正的跛脚鸭考验在亚洲
最近，我们的乔治城团队收到了大量媒体要求对涉及英伟达芯片技术曝光及其对美国国家安全影响的指控进行评论的请求。这些调查通常集中在中国情报部门如何进行间谍活动以及如何应对这些活动。
我们不会低估这种威胁。间谍活动、网络入侵和其他秘密活动是中国获取外国技术的长期特征。但我们十多年来的研究表明，这些活动仅占中国对外技术获取总体努力的一小部分——可能不是最大的一部分，也可以说不是最重要的。
相反，中国创建了一个全国性的生态系统，通过合法交易、非法活动和我们所说的“法外”转移的结合来运作：外部观察者无法获得其细节，其合法性也无法轻易确定。
由于这些不太引人注目的做法缺乏传统间谍活动的耸人听闻的吸引力，因此它们很少受到类似的关注。其结果是公众对中国技术获取体系的理解被扭曲，以及用于对抗该体系的资源的错误配置。
中国对外国技术的追求既不新鲜也不神秘。自 1949 年中华人民共和国成立以来，北京一直在运营完善的基础设施，用于识别、获取外国技术进步并将其改造为国内使用。
该企业包括政府部委、科研机构、商业实体、技术转移中心、专业协会、海外实验室以及旨在招募具有专业知识的科学家和工程师的项目。
它的前身可以追溯到19世纪中国努力获取西方技术，同时保留其国内政治和社会制度。历届中国政府都将这些努力正式化。其目标不仅仅是复制发明，而是利用知识产生商业和战略上有用的结果。
出于分析目的，我们将外国技术获取分为三大类。
合法转让包括购买技术、收购外国公司、联合研究、投资初创企业、海外实验室、大学合作以及招聘科研人员。这些交易本质上并不是不正当的。然而，交易可能是合法的，同时也存在战略风险。
非法转让包括传统间谍活动、网络盗窃、违反保密协议、盗窃商业秘密、所谓的“蜜罐”活动以及法律禁止的其他活动。这些是酒吧最熟悉的做法
